passages.title: The value of research into mite harvestmen
content: Few people have heard of the mite harvestman, and fewer still would recognize it at close range. The insect is a relative of the far more familiar daddy longlegs. But its legs are stubby rather than long, and its body is only as big as a sesame seed. To find mite harvestmen, scientists go to dark, humid forests and sift through the leaf litter. The animals respond by turning motionless, making them impossible for even a trained eye to pick out.’ They look like grains of dirt.’ said Gonzalo Giribet, an invertebrate biologist at Harvard University.

Dr Giribet and his colleagues have spent six years searching for mite harvestmen on five continents. The animals have an extraordinary story to tell - they carry a record of hundreds of millions of years of geological history, chronicling the journeys that continents have made around the Earth. The Earth’s landmasses have slowly collided and broken apart again several times, carrying animals and plants with them. These species have provided clues to the continents’ paths.

The notion of continental drift originally came from such clues. In 1911, the German scientist Alfred Wegener was struck by the fact that fossils of similar animals and plants could be found on either side of the Atlantic. The ocean was too big for the species to have traveled across it on their own. Wegener speculated correctly, as it turned out that the surrounding continents had originally been welded together in a single landmass, which he called Pangea.

Continental drift, or plate tectonics as it is scientifically known, helped move species around the world. Armadillos and their relatives are found in South America and Africa today because their ancestors evolved when the continents were joined. When South America and North America connected a few million years ago, armadillos spread north, too.

Biogeographers can learn clues about continental drift by comparing related species. However, they must also recognize cases where species have spread for other reasons, such as by crossing great stretches of water. The island of Hawaii, for example, was home to a giant flightless goose that has become extinct. Studies on DNA extracted from its bones show that it evolved from the Canada goose. Having colonized Hawaii, it branched off from that species, losing its ability to fly. This evolution occurred half a million years ago, when geologists estimate that Hawaii emerged from the Pacific.

When species jump around the planet, their histories blur. It is difficult to say much about where cockroaches evolved, for example, because they can move quickly from continent to continent. This process, known as dispersal, limits many studies. ‘Most of them tend to concentrate on particular parts of the world.' Dr Giribet said. I wanted to find a new system for studying biogeography on a global scale.

Dr Giribet realized that mite harvestmen might be that system. The 5,000 or so mite harvestmen species can be found on every continent except Antarctica. Unlike creatures found around the world like cockroaches, mite harvestmen cannot disperse well. The typical harvestman species has a range of fewer than 50 miles. Harvestmen are not found on young islands like Hawaii, as these types of islands emerged long after the break-up of Pangea.

According to Assistant Professor Sarah Boyer, a former student of Dr Giribet. ‘It’s really hard to find a group of species that is distributed all over the world but that also doesn’t disperse very far.'

What mite harvestmen lack in mobility, they make up in age. Their ancestors were among the first land animals, and fossils of daddy longlegs have been found in 400 million-year-ago rocks. Mite harvestmen evolved long before Pangea broke up and have been carried along by continental drift ever since they’ve managed to get themselves around the world only because they’ve been around for hundreds of millions of years, Dr Boyer said. Dr Boyer, Dr Giribet and their colleagues have gathered thousands of mite harvestmen from around the world, from which they extracted DNA. Variations in the genes helped the scientists build an evolutionary tree. By calculating how quickly the DNA mutated, the scientists could estimate when lineages branched off. They then compared the harvestmen's evolution to the movements of the continents. ‘The patterns are remarkably clear.’ Dr Boyer said.

The scientists found that they could trace mite harvestmen from their ancestors on Pangea. One lineage includes species in Chile South Africa, Sri Lanka and other places separated by thousands of miles of ocean. But 150 million years ago, all those sites were in Gondwana which was a region of Pangea.

The harvestmen preserve smaller patterns of continental drift, as well as bigger ones. After analyzing the DNA of a Florida harvestman, Metasiro americanus, the scientists were surprised to find that it was not related to other North American species. Its closet relatives live in West Africa. Dr Boyer then began investigating the geological history of Florida and found recent research to explain the mystery. Florida started out welded to West Africa near Segenal. North America than collied into them Pangea was forming. About 170 million years ago, North America ripped away from West Africa, taking Florida with it. The African ancestors of Florida’s harvestmen came along the ride.
Dr Giribet now hopes to study dozens or even hundreds of species, to find clues about plate tectonics that a single animal could not show.

passages.title: Apartments in Arillas
content: ApartmentsParkingAdditional InformationRose Garden ApartmentsExample: free parking lota large [ _____ ]Blue Bayno parking lotman-made lake, no [ _____ ]Sunshade Apartmentshuge parking lotNo [ _____ ] In the roomGrand Apartmentsno charge on streetmost guests are [ _____ ]
transcript: [00:39] Receptionist: Greek Island Holidays, can I help you?
[00:42] Tourist: Yes, I hope so. I have a friend who's just come back from Corfu, and she's recommended some apartments in Arilas. She thought they might be on your list.
[00:52] Receptionist: Arilas, mmm, let me check. Can you give me the names?
[00:57] Tourist: Yes. The first is Rose Garden Apartments. Could you tell me a little bit of information about the apartments? Its features and prices, for instance?
[01:07] Receptionist: Well, at Rose Garden, they have a huge parking lot, and it is free parking. So it can be very convenient for some big families who drive there to spend holidays.
[01:18] Tourist: Oh, that's great. Our whole family will be going.
[01:22] Receptionist: And there's a big swimming pool inside, which can accommodate over 50 people. We are thinking of replacing it into an aquarium, but it's still in discussion.
[01:32] Tourist: That sounds exciting. What about the cost?
[01:35] Receptionist: Two hundred and nineteen dollars.
[01:37] Tourist: That seems reasonable. I'm just jotting down some notes. Now, the second one my friend mentioned was called Blue Bay.
[01:44] Receptionist: Blue Bay? Oh, yes. In fact, that's very popular, and it has some special features.
[01:51] Tourist: Really?
[01:51] Receptionist: The main attraction is the large man-made lake, and it's only around a kilometer from some shops.
[01:57] Tourist: Is it much more expensive than the first one?

[02:00] Receptionist: Actually, it's fifty dollars cheaper than the first one. That's mainly because they don't have a parking lot there. Moreover, we plan to install a lift, but we are currently short of funds, so we don't have it at the moment, and this apartment isn't really suitable for those with disabilities.
[02:19] Tourist: Right. Now there are just two more apartments on the list. The third one is Sunshade Apartments.

[02:26] Receptionist: This one is on top of a hill, with a huge parking lot. Each room used to have a nice kitchen, but we have turned it into a beautiful garden, since our customers don't cook much, and they have shared barbecue facilities.
[02:41] Tourist: Sounds great.
[02:43] Receptionist: Yes, it is well-equipped.
[02:45] Tourist: How much does it cost?
[02:47] Receptionist: Four hundred and ninety dollars.
[02:49] Tourist: I don't think that would be within our budget, unfortunately. And the last one sounds a bit expensive, too. The Grand Apartments.

[02:57] Receptionist: That one is quite reasonable. There's no parking lot, but parking on the street requires no charge. Many teenagers and businessmen have come here to spend their summer holiday, but children make the biggest part of our customers. There is a huge painting room for them.
[03:15] Tourist: Sounds lovely. OK, I will think about which one to book with my family.
[04:08] Receptionist: That's fine. We've got plenty of apartments here when you come. Is there anything else you need to know about accommodation?
[04:17] Tourist: Oh, actually, could you tell me some more details about Orillas in general?
[04:20] Receptionist: Sure. What would you like to know?
[04:23] Tourist: Well, my friend told me that Orillas was pretty, but I don't know what the best way is to see the town.

[04:29] Receptionist: Well, if you want to enjoy the scenery, then the Blue City Bus is recommended. Just a second while I check. Ah, that one is a business route, mainly for commuters. The green one is a double-decker which offers a nicer view.
[04:45] Tourist: I also heard that the ferry boat trip is quite popular.

[04:48] Receptionist: Yes, if you want to immerse yourself in the magnificent sea views, then the ferry boat trip is a must. The trip used to last 35 minutes, but we made it a little bit longer to 50 minutes in response to our customers' demands. A 30-minute seafood dinner is included in this trip.
[05:07] Tourist: Okay, and one more question. I like riding bikes. Can I rent a bike and cycle around the town?
[05:14] Receptionist: Of course. There is a mall on Main Street and Orillas Bike Hire is located behind it.
[05:20] Tourist: Okay, I have made a note of that.
[05:23] Receptionist: Furthermore, I'd like to suggest three famous museums, from which you can learn native history and culture.
[05:31] Tourist: That sounds fun.
[05:32] Receptionist: Okay, the first one has an exhibition of the interior design as well as some famous paintings and sculptures. Some of the paintings are donated by some well-known scientists.
[05:45] Tourist: That's great.

[05:46] Receptionist: Yeah, the second one is about something that is familiar to us, but actually most people don't know much about it, which is fizzy drinks or soda. The visitors will be shown the history of some famous products in this industry and how they are produced. It's interesting to know that some products have been taken to the space before.
[06:08] Tourist: Wow, I would like to go there.

[06:10] Receptionist: Yes, you should. And the last one is about some special phenomena outside the planet where we live. Some experts are there to unveil the mystery if the visitors have any questions. Various machines and equipment are displayed inside.
[06:26] Receptionist: You can't miss it. Are there any more questions for now?
[06:30] Tourist: No, that is all.
[06:32] Receptionist: I hope you have a happy journey.
[06:34] Tourist: Thank you.

passages.title: A skiing resort
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "A skiing resort"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:46] AUDIO: Hello all, welcome to Aspen Ski Resort near Cumbria. It is one of my favourite vacation spots. I first discovered this fantastic resort when it was recommended to me by a journalist who was interviewing me. I then contacted my travel agent for further information about the resort and from the first time I visited the place, it was love at first sight.

[01:13] AUDIO: Now, when I don't have acting jobs to do, I would come here and relax. My parents were both geographers and their profession afforded my siblings and I the opportunity to travel with them all over the world when we were growing up, visiting some of the places I had seen in the television documentaries I had watched. Their passion kept affecting me and eventually I realised that travelling has been something I love for a long time. A bit of background on the Aspen Ski Resort.

[01:47] AUDIO: The area of Cumbria was first known as a vacation spot in the 1920s, however that was only as a summer vacation spot. The area became home to a summer resort in the 1930s. In the 1960s, with the increasing popularity of downhill skiing, the first British ski resort appeared. The Aspen Ski Resort was established soon after in 1968 and the Cumbria area became a popular destination for winter skiing vacations.

[02:25] AUDIO: Although snow skiing is the most popular winter activity at the resort, there are also some other popular activities. In the spring, summer and fall seasons, playing golf is easily the favourite activity of most of the resort's guests. There are five top-ranked courses within a short driving distance of the resort and the resort offers many packages for visitors during the warmer months. Also, throughout the year many of the resort's guests like to visit the Great Waters Brewing Company.

[03:01] AUDIO: But it is under reconstruction at the moment. Also, many of our visitors take advantage of skydiving activities offered by a skydiving school, but the school is located in another town which is about a two-hour drive from here. Some people ask what activities are recommended in the nearby Edinburgh region. Many visitors to that popular destination often also visit either the hot springs near the city of Marlborough or the local market in the city of Jamestown.

[03:37] AUDIO: The hot springs are geothermally heated groundwaters that rise from the crust of the earth and are enjoyed by folks of all ages. However, the price of having a hot spa there is quite high this season. The Edinburgh Nature Museum is a great alternative. You will see details of the animals which are native to the area.

[04:03] AUDIO: Most visitors in the past gave really positive feedback about the museum. The market in Jamestown region has a nice selection of fruits and vegetables which are grown on farms in the area and also a selection of fresh seafood. The market is not open this week. Please note that the Aspen Resort sponsors monthly education and entertainment programmes which are open to the public.

[04:32] AUDIO: Previous programmes have featured mountain walking in Europe and wildlife around the world. The upcoming entertainment programme which will take place at 7pm May 18th in the resort's conference centre will be about the landscape of the United Kingdom. These events are free to those attending but seats are available on a first-come first-served basis. Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.

[05:24] AUDIO: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20. Finally, let me outline what some of the Cumbria area's other skiing locations are popular for. Lakeside is the oldest of the area resorts. Its popularity barely decreases over the years and it was recently renovated.

[05:48] AUDIO: A newly built ski school there has attracted some attention and it will be open to the public within a couple of months. Petersburg is well known as a training site for skiing teams. It's the home training base for Olympic champion Billy Randolph. Winterton is a resort that is well known as a place for inexperienced skiers.

[06:13] AUDIO: It has many different bunny hills for new learners and it doesn't require any good equipment. Al's Slops is a resort that will provide you with some special service. They have a certified staff that will care for your kids while you're on the slopes. For people who want to enjoy the beauty of nature as well as having some exciting activities, these places are.

passages.title: A nursing course
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "A nursing course"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:51] Tutor: Helen and Paul, congratulations to you both for doing so well the past semester. You two have exhibited an impeccable performance during your first year in the nursing programme. I'd like to get some feedback from the two of you to better improve the programme and to provide guidance for our prospective students. I'd like to start with you, Helen.
[01:12] Tutor: So, first of all, which aspect of the programme impressed you?

[01:17] Helen: Well, to be honest, when I was enrolled into the course, I was expecting a group of classmates my age. But as I stepped into the classroom for the first time, I was surprised by the diversity. Most were in their 20s, but there were also those in their 30s or even 40s. As it turns out, the intergenerational communication has sparked intense debate and new thinking and I think that's something special about the programme that I appreciate very much.
[01:45] Tutor: What about you, Paul? What do you think of the programme?

[01:48] Paul: For me, the group project we carried out last semester is another key feature of the programme. The whole class was divided into eight different groups working on eight prospective cases. Team building sessions were conducted in a collaborative way most of the time. Comprised of five members, our group studied acute pancreatitis.

[02:11] Paul: During the process, we broke the task into different parts and assigned them to each member. We were then able to tackle the complex problem by pooling our knowledge and skills. More importantly, stronger links were established between the group members. Because of the project, we've all become good friends.

[02:31] Tutor: That's true. According to graduates, group projects prepare them for the work world in which teamwork and collaboration are increasingly the norm. So tell me, Paul, what else do you like about the programme?

[02:44] Paul: I want to be a registered nurse working in a public hospital after graduation. So the internship provided is a valuable opportunity for clinical practice in a supportive learning atmosphere. However, I was amazed by the amount of written assignments since I thought the course should have focused more on practice-oriented learning.

[03:05] Helen: Well, I have to disagree with you, Paul. The essays demonstrate your understanding of the course. For me, writing essays is a process that involves critical thinking, which challenges me to develop my points more thoroughly. I thus manage to gain a diversity of perspectives.

[03:23] Tutor: The programme is designed to deliver basic and advanced theoretical knowledge of core concepts, including healthcare systems concepts, together with practicum or clinical practice experience to bridge the classroom content to the practice setting. So I'm afraid written work is unavoidable. Also this year, we've added a module of law. How do you feel about that?
[03:48] Helen: At first, we felt that learning law is kind of redundant and too time-consuming. After a few sessions, we realised that it is necessary in dealing with future medical disputes.
[04:36] Tutor: Do you have any suggestions for prospective students?
[04:40] Paul: What bothers me most is handing in essays on time. I almost missed the deadline once because there were three essays due within the same week. So rationalising your time is critical.

[04:53] Helen: Well, that's true. The lectures deliver so much useful information. I have poor memory, so I kept making notes and revisiting them on a regular basis. To my surprise, at the end of the semester I have learnt the key concepts by heart.
[05:08] Tutor: How was the research? I heard that it was quite challenging. How did you manage to overcome the difficulties?

[05:14] Paul: That's true. The majority of us had no clue how to carry out the research at first. Fortunately, when I was digging up reference materials at the library, I sought help from the librarian. She taught me about finding the appropriate resources and choosing the proper research methods.
[05:32] Tutor: Have you checked out the online forum?

[05:34] Helen: Yes. It has become a habit for me to visit the forum regularly, in a sense. It extends classroom learning. It is where the students post academic problems that they come across and get support from the faculty members.
[05:48] Paul: Some of my classmates didn't do so well during the placement tests. I feel that background reading is necessary.
[05:55] Tutor: Lastly, do you have anything to say to the freshmen?

[05:59] Helen: I was really ambitious at first, trying to get straight A's on my transcript. I made tons of notes and worked hard, even on the optional assignments, to get extra credit. I stressed myself out before having an emotional breakdown. After consulting my advisor, I found it important to set realistic goals.
[06:18] Helen: Don't push yourself too hard. It is wise to sort out your priorities.
[06:24] Tutor: Thank you for coming here today and providing valuable feedback on the programme. Have a great summer break.

explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: don't set unrealistic goals

passages.title: Dinner Affects the Environment
content: 📌 Dinner Affects the Environment
Food industry
- The amount of CO2 from producing our daily meals is the same as that from [ _____ ]
- The process of making 100g [ _____ ] beans can result in 140g CO2.
- The [ _____ ] production process contributes to climate & warming emissions.
- Scientists are working on reducing the impact of [ _____ ] process.
- Packaging needs [ _____ ] as well as water and other resources for production.
- Long distance [ _____ ] leads to more pollution.
- Due to the damage of [ _____ ] the total amount of CO2 increases greatly
Agriculture
- Livestock are either kept on farms or on a [ _____ ] in different parts of the world.
- In animal agriculture, [ _____ ] required constantly
- Some agricultural activities like[ _____ ] are unlikely to be changed
transcript: [01:13] AUDIO: Good afternoon, thanks for coming to today's lecture. In the last few decades the environmental impact of food production and consumption has become one of the greatest concerns. When we look at what we eat and how we produce the food we can find extensive evidence for how we damage our environment. Greenhouse gas emissions may come from livestock such as cows, agricultural soils and rice production.

[01:38] AUDIO: According to statistics, the carbon dioxide emissions from the production of the food people consume every day are almost the same as the emissions we make when we are driving. Let's look at some more specific examples. The cultivation and processing of 100 grams of coffee beans are responsible for 140 grams of carbon dioxide. Now, some international organizations are training farmers in many countries to use sustainable agricultural methods as a way of reducing their carbon dioxide emissions.

[02:11] AUDIO: All agricultural practices have been found to have a variety of effects on the environment. Some of the environmental effects are associated with meat production. The popular red meat requires 28 times more land to produce than chicken, 11 times more water and results in 5 times more climate warming emissions. According to another research, cooking process also causes greenhouse gas emissions.

[02:38] AUDIO: Scientists now are working on how to best minimize its impact. Another problem that we cannot neglect is the packaging of food products, as packaging takes a lot of energy, water and other natural resources to produce. So, a lot of natural resources are wasted when we throw the packaging materials away. Furthermore, packaging waste produces a big amount of greenhouse gas.

[03:04] AUDIO: To make things even worse, the food we eat often comes from places far away. Therefore, the transportation of our food across long distances contributes to air and water pollution. In recent decades, with the growing number of population, more food is in demand. So more land has been used to produce food.

[03:23] AUDIO: Hundreds and even thousands of forests have been cut down. It had a devastating effect on the climate because forests can absorb greenhouse gases. People in different parts of the world apply various kinds of farming practices. In most countries, cows and other livestock are kept on the farms, while in some countries they are kept in a restricted area on a mountain.

[03:50] AUDIO: But they all contribute to the carbon dioxide emissions. And for animal agriculture, the problem can be more serious because the livestock need food all the time. In America, cows eat an overwhelming amount of corn and soybeans each year. In order to create a better world for us and our future generations, we should adopt sustainable agriculture.

[04:14] AUDIO: The goal of sustainable agriculture is to meet the world's growing demand for food at the present without affecting future generations. Every person involved in the food system, growers, food processors, distributors, retailers, consumers and waste managers can play a role in ensuring a sustainable agricultural system. There are many practices commonly used by people working in sustainable agriculture and sustainable food systems. Crop growers may change their food production methods to prevent pollution, although some other areas of agriculture are very hard to change, such as fishing.

[04:51] AUDIO: Consumers and retailers concerned with sustainability can look for foods that are environmentally friendly. However, sustainable agriculture is more than a collection of practices. It is also a process of negotiation, a push and pull between the competing interests of an individual farmer or of people in a community as they work to solve complex problems about how we grow our food. In conclusion, I want to emphasize that we may not be able to go back to the old times and live a simpler lifestyle, but we can take an active role in preventing more environmental problems caused by carbon dioxide emissions.
[05:29] AUDIO: In the next lecture, I will share some of the studies and effective solutions with you.

questions.prompt: - The amount of CO2 from producing our daily meals is the same as that from _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "According to statistics, the carbon dioxide emissions from the production of the food people consume every day are almost the same as the emissions we make when we are driving."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “According to statistics, the carbon dioxide emissions from the production of the food people consume every day…” (00:01:38) ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi nói: “The amount of CO2 from producing our daily meals is the same as that from…” → Nghe kỹ, ta thấy câu trong bài là: “…are almost the same as the emissions we make when we are driving.” → "we are driving" chính là hoạt động được so sánh với việc sản xuất bữa ăn. → Danh từ cần điền là “ driving ”. ✅ Đáp án đúng : driving 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ car => Sai vì trong bài không nhắc đến “car” – mà là hành động “driving”. Nếu viết “car” sẽ sai về dạng từ. ❌ transport => Sai vì “transport” không được nói cụ thể ở đây – chỉ có “driving” được nêu rõ và được dùng
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: driving

questions.prompt: - The process of making 100g _____ beans can result in 140g CO2.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The cultivation and processing of 100 grams of coffee beans are responsible for 140 grams of carbon dioxide."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “The cultivation and processing of 100 grams of…” (00:01:52) ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi yêu cầu tìm loại thực phẩm được sản xuất với lượng CO2 là 140g cho mỗi 100g. → Nghe kỹ đoạn: “The cultivation and processing of 100 grams of coffee beans are responsible for 140 grams of carbon dioxide.” → Từ khóa cần điền là “ coffee ” (vì “beans” đã có sẵn trong đề). ✅ Đáp án đúng : coffee 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ cocoa => Sai vì không nhắc đến trong bài. ❌ beans => Sai vì đã được cho sẵn trong đề rồi – ta chỉ cần điền loại hạt nào (coffee). ❌ food => Sai vì không cụ thể, không khớp với số liệu 140g CO2 như trong bài.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: coffee

questions.prompt: - The _____ production process contributes to climate & warming emissions.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Some of the environmental effects are associated with meat production. The popular red meat requires 28 times more land to produce than chicken, 11 times more water and results in 5 times more climate warming emissions."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Some of the environmental effects are associated with…” (00:02:16) ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi muốn biết loại quy trình sản xuất nào góp phần gây biến đổi khí hậu . → Nghe kỹ đoạn: “Some of the environmental effects are associated with meat production. The popular red meat requires 28 times more land... and results in 5 times more climate warming emissions.” → Ở đây, “ meat production” (đặc biệt là thịt đỏ) được nói đến rõ ràng là góp phần làm tăng lượng khí gây nóng lên toàn cầu (climate warming emissions). ✅ Đáp án đúng : meat 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ dairy => Không hề được nhắc đến trong đoạn này. ❌ food => Quá chung chung, không sát nghĩa như “meat”. ❌ red => Sai vì đây là tính từ bổ nghĩa cho “meat”,
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: meat

questions.prompt: - Scientists are working on reducing the impact of _____ process.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "According to another research, cooking process also causes greenhouse gas emissions."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “According to another research, cooking process also causes greenhouse gas emissions. Scientists now are working on how to best minimize its impact.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Câu hỏi hỏi về quy trình mà các nhà khoa học đang cố gắng giảm tác động của nó. – Trong bài nghe, cụm "cooking process also causes greenhouse gas emissions" (quá trình nấu ăn cũng tạo ra khí nhà kính) chính là thông tin chính. – Ngay sau đó, người nói nói: "Scientists now are working on how to best minimize its impact." → Điều này chứng minh rằng từ cần điền là cooking , vì đó là quá trình mà các nhà khoa học đang tìm cách giảm tác động. ✅ Đáp án đúng : cooking 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ eating => Không đúng vì bài nghe không đề cập đến việ
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: cooking

questions.prompt: - Packaging needs _____ as well as water and other resources for production.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Another problem that we cannot neglect is the packaging of food products, as packaging takes a lot of energy, water and other natural resources to produce."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Another problem that we cannot neglect is the packaging of food products, as packaging takes a lot of energy, water and other natural resources to produce.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Câu hỏi yêu cầu tìm một yếu tố cần thiết cùng với water và resources để sản xuất bao bì. – Trong bài nghe, cụm "packaging takes a lot of energy, water and other natural resources" cho ta đáp án. → Ta thấy energy là từ xuất hiện đầu tiên và được liệt kê cùng với water và resources , nên đây chính là từ cần điền. ✅ Đáp án đúng : energy 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ electricity => Dễ nhầm vì nó cũng là một dạng năng lượng, nhưng trong bài nghe không nói cụ thể “electricity” mà là energy – từ tổng quát hơn. ❌ fuel => Cũng là một dạng năng
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: energy

questions.prompt: - Long distance _____ leads to more pollution.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Therefore, the transportation of our food across long distances contributes to air and water pollution."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “To make things even worse, the food we eat often comes from places far away. Therefore, the transportation of our food across long distances contributes to air and water pollution.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Từ khóa trong đề là “long distance ... leads to more pollution” , và trong bài nghe, thông tin xuất hiện rất rõ: "the transportation of our food across long distances contributes to air and water pollution" → transportation chính là hoạt động gây ô nhiễm do khoảng cách xa. ✅ Đáp án đúng : transportation 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ delivery => Tuy đúng nghĩa, nhưng không xuất hiện trong bài nghe. ❌ shipping => Cũng là một hình thức vận chuyển, nhưng từ khóa chính xác trong bài là transportation – được dùng bao
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: transportation

questions.prompt: - Due to the damage of _____ the total amount of CO2 increases greatly

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Hundreds and even thousands of forests have been cut down. It had a devastating effect on the climate because forests can absorb greenhouse gases."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Hundreds and even thousands of forests have been cut down. It had a devastating effect on the climate because forests can absorb greenhouse gases.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Trong câu hỏi: “Due to the damage of ______, the total amount of CO2 increases greatly.” – Trong bài nghe, người nói nhấn mạnh việc “ forests have been cut down” và hậu quả là “ it had a devastating effect on the climate because forests can absorb greenhouse gases.” → Suy ra, việc phá rừng (damage of forests) là nguyên nhân làm lượng CO2 tăng cao. ✅ Đáp án đúng : forests 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ trees => Mặc dù đúng về nghĩa, nhưng từ được dùng trong bài là forests , bao gồm cả hệ sinh thái rộng lớn hơn cây riêng lẻ. ❌ land => Không đúng,
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: forests

questions.prompt: - Livestock are either kept on farms or on a _____ in different parts of the world.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "In most countries, cows and other livestock are kept on the farms, while in some countries they are kept in a restricted area on a mountain."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “In most countries, cows and other livestock are kept on the farms, while in some countries they are kept in a restricted area on a mountain .” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Câu hỏi yêu cầu: “Livestock are either kept on farms or on a ______ in different parts of the world.” – Trong bài nghe, người nói: “kept on the farms” hoặc “in a restricted area on a mountain .” → “mountain” là từ được nhấn mạnh ở đây như một nơi đặc biệt khác với farm . ✅ Đáp án đúng : mountain 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ hill => Dễ nhầm vì liên quan đến địa hình cao, nhưng từ trong bài là “mountain”, không phải “hill”. ❌ field => “field” gần nghĩa với “farm”, không phải phương án thay thế hợp lý ở đây.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: mountain

questions.prompt: - In animal agriculture, _____ required constantly

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And for animal agriculture, the problem can be more serious because the livestock need food all the time."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “...the livestock need food all the time.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Câu hỏi hỏi: “In animal agriculture, ______ is required constantly.” – Trong bài nghe, người nói rất rõ: “the livestock need food all the time” → Đây chính là đáp án vì food là thứ được yêu cầu một cách “constantly” (liên tục). ✅ Đáp án đúng : food 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ water => Không được nhắc đến trong ngữ cảnh này. ❌ space => Dù có thể cần thiết, nhưng bài nghe không đề cập đến yếu tố này trong câu liên quan.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: food

questions.prompt: - Some agricultural activities like_____ are unlikely to be changed

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Crop growers may change their food production methods to prevent pollution, although some other areas of agriculture are very hard to change, such as fishing."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “...some other areas of agriculture are very hard to change, such as fishing .” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Câu hỏi hỏi: “Some agricultural activities like ______ are unlikely to be changed.” – Trong bài nghe, có một câu rõ ràng: “some other areas of agriculture are very hard to change, such as fishing .” → Từ “fishing” chính là ví dụ cụ thể cho một hoạt động khó thay đổi. ✅ Đáp án đúng : fishing 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ farming => Đây là khái niệm chung, không phải một ví dụ cụ thể như “fishing”. ❌ breeding => Không được đề cập trong đoạn đó, nên không chính xác.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: fishing

passages.title: Manor Farm
content:
📌 MANOR FARM
Application Form – Summer Fruit Picking

Name:                               Ben Miller
Country of origin:           the USA
Age:                                   20
Visa type:                         a [ _____ ]
Visa valid until:               November
Availability for work:     from [ _____ ] to October
Heard about job:             from the [ _____ ]

📌 MANOR FARM
Important information for fruit picker

Picking season:
Busiest month is [ _____ ].
Exact picking dates depend on the [ _____ ].

Payment:
Pickers over 18 will earn £[ _____ ]  an hour.

Accommodation:
None on the farm but there is a [ _____ ] nearby.

Transport:
Pickers are advised to travel around by [ _____ ]

Documentation:
Only pickers with a [ _____ ] will be allowed to work.

Meals:
Pickers must bring lunch and a day’s supply of [ _____ ]
transcript: [02:27] Woman: Manor Farm. Hello.
[02:29] Ben: Hi there. I'd like to apply to do fruit picking this summer.
[02:32] Woman: Oh, hello. I'm Mrs. Chandler. My husband and I own Manor Farm. Let me take some details.
[02:40] Woman: I'll just get a form to fill in. Hold on.
[02:44] Ben: Sure.
[02:46] Woman: Sorry. Right. Your name is...
[02:50] Ben: It's Ben Miller.
[02:52] Woman: And where are you from?
[02:54] Ben: I'm from the USA.
[02:56] Woman: Fine. Mmm, can I ask your age?
[03:00] Ben: I'm 20. You only take people over the age of 16, don't you?
[03:05] Woman: Yes, that's right. Are you able to work in the UK?
[03:09] Ben: Sorry?
[03:10] Woman: I mean, do you have a visa?
[03:12] Ben: Oh, yeah. I have a thing called a blue card. It's valid until November.
[03:18] Woman: That's fine, then. We'll need fruit pickers from the middle of June until the end of September. What's your availability?
[03:27] Ben: When can I work? Mmm, I'd like to do July, August and September, and could do October if there's any work then.
[03:36] Woman: Okay. Did you find out about us through our website?
[03:41] Ben: That's right. It's much easier than going through an agency. I see you need most pickers in September for apples and pears, but the whole picking season can last about 16 weeks.
[04:45] Woman: Well, yes, but it's a question of the weather. That determines how much fruit we grow, of course. That's why I can't give you exact picking dates now.
[04:55] Ben: I see. Oh, well, no problem. Can you tell me what pickers earn?
[05:00] Woman: Well, that depends on age. The rate is £4.50 an hour for the under-18s, but as you're over 18, it would rise to £5.60 an hour.
[05:13] Ben: Uh-huh. Your website says that you don't provide accommodation for pickers, so I guess I should arrange that in advance.
[05:21] Woman: Yes. There is no accommodation on the farm, but there is a campsite about 15 minutes away.
[05:28] Ben: Is that walking distance? What do you think? No, maybe I should bring my bike to get around.
[05:36] Woman: Yes, we always recommend that. Some pickers bring a car, but then find the roads rather narrow, and the bus is very infrequent. Do you have any questions?
[05:50] Ben: I know that fruit picking is hard work, but is there anything special I need to bring with me?
[05:55] Woman: Well, firstly, documentation is extremely important. We will need proof of age, so we'll expect to see your passport. Pickers without one won't be allowed to work.
[06:07] Ben: Oh, even if their age is written on their driving license?
[06:11] Woman: Sorry, a driving license isn't suitable.
[06:14] Ben: Fair enough. I guess some lunch is provided for all the hungry fruit pickers.
[06:20] Woman: I'm afraid not. You'll need to bring your own food for lunch, and more importantly, enough water to last a full day. It can get very hot, so drinking is vital.
[06:32] Ben: Right, like back home. Okay, well, thanks for all the information. What happens now?
[06:40] Woman: Well, I'll post a contract to you...

Thông tin cần nghe là loại giấy tờ chứng minh Ben được phép làm việc ở Anh . ✅ Đáp án đúng : blue card ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn người phụ nữ hỏi về khả năng làm việc ở UK, đặc biệt là câu “I mean, do you have a visa?” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và chốt keyword: visa / able to work in the UK ⇒ chắc chắn cần tên giấy tờ . Trong bài nghe, ngay sau câu hỏi “do you have a visa?” , Ben trả lời: “I have a thing called a blue card.” Cụm a thing called báo hiệu tên chính xác của loại giấy tờ sẽ xuất hiện ngay sau đó. Vì vậy, điền blue card là đúng. 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ July => là thông

explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: July

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.

Thông tin liên quan đến thời điểm cần nhiều người hái nhất cho apples and pears ⇒ một tháng bận nhất trong mùa hái . ✅ Đáp án đúng : September ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : câu Ben nói về when you need most pickers và nhắc đến apples and pears . ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Trước khi nghe, gạch chân các từ khóa Busiest month -> tập trung thời gian cao điểm . Khi nghe, Ben nói rõ: cần nhiều người hái nhất ( need most pickers in September) cho apples and pears . explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "I see you need most pickers in September for apples and pears, but the whole picking season can last about 16 weeks. Well, yes, but it's a question of the weather. That determines how much fruit we grow, of course. That's why I can't give you exact picking dates now."
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : Exact picking dates depend on the _______. 🎯 Xác định loại từ cần điền : Sau cụm depend on the cần một danh từ (thường là một yếu tố/điều kiện ). Nội dung đang nói về lịch/ thời điểm hái quả ⇒ dự đoán là yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian bắt đầu/kết thúc mùa hái (ví dụ: điều kiện tự nhiên). ✅ Đáp án đúng : weather ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn Ben nói về việc mùa hái có thể kéo dài 16 tuần và hỏi về thời gian hái cụ thể ( September… apples and pears… 16 weeks ). ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa: exact picking dates và depend on ⇒ cần nghe “yếu tố quyết định lịch hái”. Trong bài nghe, người phụ nữ trả lời: “it’s a question of the weather ” . Cụm it’s a question of mang nghĩa “phụ thuộc vào/ do … quyết định”, tương ứn

explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : Pickers over 18 will earn £_______ an hour. 🎯 Xác định loại từ cần điền : Sau ký hiệu £ cần điền một con số/ số thập phân để chỉ mức lương theo giờ . Cụm over 18 cho thấy thông tin cần nghe là mức lương cho người trên 18 tuổi (cao hơn mức của under-18s). ✅ Đáp án đúng : 5.6 ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn Ben hỏi về tiền công – câu hỏi kiểu “Can you tell me what pickers earn?” và người phụ nữ trả lời “that depends on age” . ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và gạch chân các từ khóa: rate , £4.50 , under-18s , over 18 , rise to . Khi nghe thấy cụm depends on age , bạn biết ngay sau đó sẽ có hai mức lương theo độ tuổi. Bài nghe nói rõ: “£4.50 an hour for the under-18s” (mức thấp hơn), rồi chuyển ý bằng “but as you're over 18” . Sau cụm

passages.title: Karrara Sports & Leisure Centre
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Karrara Sports & Leisure Centre"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:59] AUDIO: Good evening and welcome to Carrara's brand new Sports and Leisure Centre. First I'll tell you about our facilities, then feel free to wander around the centre. Now as you can see from the map I've given you, we're sitting in our cafe, which we hope will be a favourite place to visit after exercising. To one side of us, and right in front of you as you enter the complex, is the shop.

[01:26] AUDIO: Be sure to have a look in there later as we've got some great opening specials on footwear. On the other side of the cafe, and ideally situated between the cafe and the child-minding facilities, we have the playground. You can sit and relax there while your kids have a great time on the equipment. And our childcare facilities are available to anyone using the centre.

[01:52] AUDIO: Let's talk a little bit about our heated swimming pool, which is also near the entrance on the other side from the cafe. It has a five-metre water slide, which will be very popular with kids of all ages, and in the corner, nearest the changing rooms, we have a high-tech hot spa. The water is heated to 38 degrees centigrade, which is the ideal temperature to relax tired muscles after a workout. So, where can you do these workouts?

[02:22] AUDIO: Well, we have a large weights room located at the cafe end of the administration block. In the weights room, you'll find all the latest equipment. We also have trainers there who can put a program together for you. Another place to get a good workout is in the gym, which is shown on the map to the right of the changing rooms.

[02:46] AUDIO: There will be all sorts of classes offered there. Our aim is to provide all your exercise and recovery needs. So, as well as the spa to help aching bodies, we also have a special area for massage. It's in the funny-shaped room close to the administration area.

[03:06] AUDIO: Its distinctive shape has already led to the nickname of the bullet room. We'll be offering Swedish and Chinese massage there, and we'll offer physiotherapy in the future. Now, let me tell you something about our different memberships. Firstly, we offer different types of membership to cater for different needs.

[04:06] AUDIO: If you are a fitness freak, then choose our all-in membership. This gives you access to everything in the centre, all the classes and sports. It's usually our most expensive option, but for a short time, we're offering 12 months for the price of nine, which is a huge saving. If you prefer just the gym classes, you may want to consider the gym and weights package.

[04:32] AUDIO: It works out at $10 a week, which is good value. If you just want to swim, then we recommend getting a SwimPlus membership. With this, you have unlimited use of the pool and spa. The other package we've reduced for this month only is the off-peak.

[04:51] AUDIO: This is aimed at people who are happy to come at less busy times. And finally, we have the family pack. We believe in keeping the whole family fit and healthy, so this package works out cheaper than buying it separately. Your flyer has details of all the prices.

[05:10] AUDIO: So, anyone who signs up for a new membership tonight will receive two fantastic presents from us. We wanted to make these rewards something different from the norm. We could have just chosen a towel for you to use in the gym or some clothing from the shop, but we wanted to show our appreciation by giving you something special. So not only are we going to give you a voucher for a session in our massage centre, a great way to unwind after your workout, but you'll also get this great device that measures your heart rate.
[05:45] AUDIO: And finally, just for turning up tonight, we'd like to give everyone here a drink bottle to take away with them. That's all I wanted to say.

passages.title: Evaluating the Value Survey on House Prices
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Evaluating the Value Survey on House Prices"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [01:09] Tutor: OK, for this week's assignment you're going to assess the value survey on house prices. What were the survey's findings? Was it a reliable survey? Work in pairs, discuss what you've read and generate some ideas for the assignment.
[01:26] James: All right. Shall we work together, Anna?
[01:29] Anna: Sure, James. So, first, how did the value survey actually measure the cost of houses? Because there are lots of ways of calculating it.

[01:39] James: Well, it looked at all houses, didn't it? New and old. So it started with average incomes across the whole workforce and then worked out house prices in relation to that, I mean to what people were earning.
[01:51] Anna: So it's about affordability, what people pay in real terms. There's no information about the size of a house a typical family can buy.
[02:00] James: No, that's a limitation. OK, then in the assignment we should give some background. I mean, what's different about the value survey?

[02:10] Anna: Yeah, there's lots of these surveys every year. Value is actually one of the newer ones, but it stands out because it gives figures for a range of the largest urban centres, which none of the others do.
[02:22] James: OK, good point. Then one finding was that New Zealand houses are relatively expensive. Why is that? Because most of them are built of wood, and that's quite cheap.
[02:33] Anna: Yeah, it is. But the problem is there are too many regulations and restrictions about where you can build.
[02:39] James: So if more building sites were created for housing, the costs would come down. That's it, isn't it? Because there are plenty of contractors ready to do the work.
[02:49] Anna: Exactly. So, um, what else?

[02:52] James: Well, what about transport? I mean, it's all very well to talk about new housing, but how are people going to get there? Is the survey proposing new roads, new rail networks? It should be a coordinated approach.
[03:06] Anna: Yeah, but the survey didn't mention it. It's a missed opportunity because a commitment to funding public transport from the outset would improve air quality in our cities.
[03:15] James: True. OK then, the next survey, what can we expect? It'll look at all the same places, right?
[03:22] Anna: Exactly the same. But the next one will give an idea of the way prices are moving.
[03:27] James: The government may have to think about how house prices are affecting society.

[04:14] Anna: Then in the assignment, we need to evaluate how reliable the survey was, so we should look at some of the criticism made by commentators. OK, so there's the economist Andrew Coleman. He actually questioned whether the survey was money well spent because it only looked at a single year in isolation.

[04:32] James: A year when it was difficult to borrow money to buy a house, pushing up costs. So he thought the survey should consider a longer time frame. Did you get that article by Professor Massey? Because he's the leading authority on this topic.

[04:46] Anna: Yeah, interesting. He realised the method used to calculate how much money people had didn't take savings into account. So actually, people looking for a house were richer than the survey shows, making houses cheaper in real terms.

[05:00] James: Alright, then Richard Bernard. His criticism was original. He found out they were using quite outdated software to process all the information they gathered, which was crazy because they actually had the money available for an upgrade. So even though it was a highly regarded team of people, the way the statistics were interpreted was open to question.
[05:21] Anna: OK, then Professor Lowndes. He thought the report was just badly written.
[05:26] James: That's right. After all the work that went into gathering valid information, the finished report was just too long and weakly structured. And there was too much unnecessary detail.
[05:36] Anna: And the last one, Maria Darling. She made a point about the properties that were evaluated.
[05:42] James: There weren't enough of them, you mean?

[05:43] Anna: No, it wasn't that. But they were never identified for privacy reasons. But she thought the actual properties used should have been revealed, you know. The process should have been transparent if the people are going to have full confidence in the survey.
[05:57] James: Right. So a lot of criticism.
[05:59] Anna: Yeah. But this sort of research is often controversial.

passages.title: Benefits of using drama activities in the classroom
content: 📌 BENEFITS OF USING DRAMA ACTIVITIES IN THE CLASSROOM
Child’s personal development
Group participation develops [ _____ ] in their own ideas.Unscripted, imaginative activities allow children to take [ _____ ].
Child’s educational development
Working as a group teaches the importance of [ _____ ] to others.Performing makes children [ _____ ] for their learning and behavior.
Role-play can be used:

as a form of [ _____ ] for children experiencing problemsto help children be objective about their behaviour problemsto explore controversial issues with a class in a [ _____ ] environmentto explore children’s self-knowledge and understanding of [ _____ ]
Advantages of using role-play in the study of history

Drama activities increase children’s [ _____ ] in classMakes it easier for children to [ _____ ] and understand historical eventsCan find answers to [ _____ ] in history to see why certain decisions were made
transcript: [01:24] AUDIO: So now we're going to look at some of the reasons why it's beneficial to include drama activities, such as role play, in your teaching practice in a range of subject areas. There's a lot of evidence to show that drama helps a child's personal development. Firstly, creating the space for children to express themselves freely in a group situation helps to give them confidence in their own opinions and ideas. And, of course, drama activities can work especially well for shy or introverted children, who usually don't participate in other types of classroom situations.

[02:09] AUDIO: Secondly, unscripted improvisation activities, where children work from their imagination, if done in a supportive way, give children the opportunity to gain experience in taking risks and encourage them to say things that they might normally be afraid to say. Drama can also support the child's educational development. For example, the emphasis placed on cooperative activities in drama means that group members must learn the value of listening to one another. Being involved in any sort of performance which relies on everyone working together and playing their part also helps children to be responsible, not only for their learning, but for their general behavior.

[02:59] AUDIO: These are just a couple of ways in which drama can benefit a child's learning. Now I'd like to look at how role play can be such a valuable learning tool in the classroom. The value of role play for children who are having difficulties as a means of therapy is now widely accepted. The experience of doing a role play where children act out aspects of their own life without explicitly stating that it is a direct representation of their own experiences can help children to judge their own behavior in an objective way.

[03:41] AUDIO: One obvious example would be doing a role reversal with a bully role playing a victim. Because this approach doesn't involve direct confrontation, it may help the bully to see his or her behavior in a different light. More generally, role play also allows the teacher to explore potentially controversial or taboo subjects in a safe setting in which children feel at ease. It's obviously essential for children to feel they won't be criticized or judged for voicing certain views.

[04:17] AUDIO: Getting children to examine their thoughts and opinions carefully can lead to a deeper self-knowledge and a stronger awareness of morality. This is an important factor in developing social skills. Let's look at a specific subject area now and think about how drama can enrich the learning process for the study of history. Bringing characters from the past to life in the classroom by doing classroom drama activities is an easy way to improve the level of the children's participation in the lesson.

[04:53] AUDIO: So, drama in the history classroom makes for a livelier atmosphere, but getting children to reenact scenes from history can also be extremely useful as it helps them to remember what happened and why it was important, as well as helping to bring the past alive. Another way of doing this is to ask children to find solutions to historical problems using role play. This can help to focus attention on why certain decisions were taken. For example, children can be asked to decide how best to defend their town from attack or where to build a new settlement.
[05:35] AUDIO: Okay, what I'd like to do now is to think about your next teaching practice session and in groups discuss how you would incorporate an element of drama into your lesson plan.

passages.title: The International School, Dubai
content: 📌 The International School, Dubai
General Information and facilities
• Two departments: Lower school
Middle school
• Location of school opposite the [ _____ ]
• School address: Meadows Drive. Dubai
• Uniform: a [ _____ ] shirt, black trousers or shorts
• Lessons from 7.20 until [ _____ ], Sunday - Thursday
• Children on Early Start programme are given [ _____ ] before school starts
• Late Stay activities:
- playtime
- help with homework
- current term's spoil activity is [ _____ ]
• Music [ _____ ] lessons held on Tuesdays
• Languages [ _____ ] from age 7
Meeting with Head Teacher
Name of Head Teacher: Elizabeth Rose Day: [ _____ ]
Can talk to the [ _____ ] teacher in coffee break
transcript: [00:58] Man: The international school, how can I help you?
[01:01] Woman: Good morning. I was wondering if you could give me some information. I've just moved to Dubai and I have a boy of eight. I'm looking for a school for him.
[01:11] Woman: Could you give me some details about your school?

[01:14] Man: Yes, of course. The lower school takes children aged 4 to 7 and the middle school is for those aged 7 to 13. Children then go on to one of the senior schools in the area until they're 18.
[01:26] Woman: My neighbour told me you're near a golf course. Is that right?
[01:30] Man: Yes, that's right. There's one just across from us.
[01:33] Woman: Right. Could you give me the address?
[01:36] Man: Of course. We're in Meadows Drive. That's M-E-A-D-O-W-S Drive. You can't miss us.
[01:45] Woman: OK, got that. Can I ask you a few more questions?
[01:49] Man: Go right ahead.
[01:51] Woman: Does the school have a uniform at all? My son didn't have to wear one at his last school.
[01:57] Man: Yes, and it's actually quite smart. We've just changed the colour from a dark green shirt to a blue one. That's with black trousers or shorts.
[02:06] Woman: What's the school timetable like?
[02:09] Man: Well, lessons begin at 7.20 Sunday to Thursday, although we do open at 7 o'clock. Lessons finish at 12.40 and the school closes at 2.30.
[02:20] Woman: That's interesting because I leave here very early to get to work. Do you provide breakfast or does my son need to have this at home?
[02:30] Man: No, we have an early start programme and we provide that for all the children who arrive early.
[02:35] Woman: Excellent. And after school?

[02:38] Man: We have a range of activities on what we call our late stay programme. There's some playtime and help with homework, but we offer sport activities as well. For example, last term we had basketball after school and now it's swimming.
[02:53] Woman: Good. And what sort of music lessons are there?
[02:57] Man: We have an orchestra and a rock band for the older children and a junior band for the younger ones.
[03:03] Woman: My son plays the piano. Could he have lessons at the school?
[03:07] Man: Yes, we have lessons on Tuesdays after school. We also have flute on Thursdays and clarinet on Mondays.
[03:15] Woman: That's great. What about languages? My son would like to do Spanish because his grandparents are from Mexico.
[03:22] Man: No problem. He's eight, isn't he? Well, he can do that now as classes start from when the children are seven. When he's ten we offer French or German as well.
[04:05] Woman: Now, what about enrollment? Could I come along sometime and see the headteacher?
[04:10] Man: Yes, indeed. Her name's Elizabeth Rose. She's usually free to speak to parents most days.
[04:16] Woman: Well, I could come in on Wednesday next week. I usually have a free day on a Tuesday, but that's been changed for next week.
[04:25] Man: OK. Would around 9.30 suit you?
[04:28] Woman: Could we make it a bit later, say 10.15? I have a dentist appointment at 9.40.

[04:34] Man: Great. Now, the head will give you a guided tour, of course, but is there anything special you're interested in? For example, some parents are interested in speaking to the sports teacher.
[04:46] Woman: Oh, I think it would be great to have a word with the science teacher. I think that's a subject my son will be very good at.
[04:53] Man: OK. We have a break for coffee at 12, so you can do that then. I'll make a note of that. I should also tell you that on that day you'll be able to see some...

questions.prompt: • Location of school opposite the _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Could you give me some details about your school? Yes, of course. The lower school takes children aged 4 to 7 and the middle school is for those aged 7 to 13. Children then go on to one of the senior schools in the area until they're 18. My neighbour told me you're near a golf course."
explanation.step3: (vì đề bài có cụm từ "opposite the", thường là cần điền tên địa điểm hoặc tòa nhà cụ thể) ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “My neighbour told me you're near a golf course. Is that right? – Yes, that's right. There's one just across from us.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Trong đề, từ “opposite” tương đương với “across from” trong script. – Khi nghe, ta thấy người phụ nữ hỏi: "My neighbour told me you're near a golf course," và người đàn ông trả lời: "Yes, that's right. There's one just across from us." – Như vậy, thông tin rõ ràng là trường nằm đối diện golf course . ✅ Đáp án đúng : golf course 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ School => Đây là nơi cần xác định địa điểm đối diện trường, không phải bản thân trường. ❌ Meadows Drive => Đây là địa chỉ trường,
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: golf course

questions.prompt: • Uniform: a _____ shirt, black trousers or shorts

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Does the school have a uniform at all? My son didn't have to wear one at his last school. Yes, and it's actually quite smart. We've just changed the colour from a dark green shirt to a blue one."
explanation.step3: (đứng trước từ "shirt", nên chắc chắn cần nghe một màu sắc) ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “We've just changed the colour from a dark green shirt to a blue one.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Trong audio, người nói đề cập đến việc trường vừa thay đổi đồng phục từ màu "dark green" sang một màu mới là "blue". – Do đề bài hỏi về màu sắc hiện tại của áo đồng phục, đáp án phải là màu mới, tức là blue . ✅ Đáp án đúng : blue 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ dark green => Đây là màu cũ, đã được thay thế rồi, nếu không nghe kỹ học viên rất dễ bị nhầm lẫn đáp án này.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: blue

questions.prompt: • Lessons from 7.20 until _____, Sunday - Thursday

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "What's the school timetable like? Well, lessons begin at 7.20 Sunday to Thursday, although we do open at 7 o'clock. Lessons finish at 12.40 and the school closes at 2.30."
explanation.step3: (vị trí cần điền nằm sau "until", nên chắc chắn phải là một thời gian cụ thể) ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Lessons finish at 12.40 and the school closes at 2.30.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : – Khi nghe thông tin, bạn sẽ thấy đề bài hỏi rõ "Lessons from 7.20 until…". Đây là khoảng thời gian diễn ra bài học chính thức trong ngày. – Trong audio người nói khẳng định rõ: "Lessons finish at 12.40 ", tức đây là thời gian chính xác bài học kết thúc. Thời gian 2.30 là lúc trường đóng cửa, không phải lúc bài học kết thúc, nên không phù hợp. ✅ Đáp án đúng : 12.40 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ 2.30 => Đây là thời gian trường đóng cửa, không phải thời gian kết thúc bài học. Nếu nghe không kỹ, dễ bị nhầm đáp án này.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: 12.40

questions.prompt: • Children on Early Start programme are given _____ before school starts

explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Do you provide breakfast or does my son need to have this at home? No, we have an early start programme and we provide that for all the children who arrive early."
explanation.step3: ” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Người phụ nữ hỏi rõ về việc con của cô ấy cần ăn sáng ở nhà hay sẽ được cung cấp tại trường. Người đàn ông trả lời rằng họ có một chương trình đặc biệt cho trẻ đến sớm (early start programme) và nhà trường sẽ cung cấp ( provide ) thứ này. Thứ được đề cập ở đây rõ ràng là bữa sáng ( breakfast ). ✅ Đáp án đúng : breakfast 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ early start => Đây chỉ là tên của chương trình, không phải thứ được cung cấp cho học sinh. ❌ homework, snack hoặc meals => Audio không nhắc tới các từ này, học sinh nếu không tập trung có thể nghe sai đáp án.

questions.prompt: - current term's spoil activity is _____

Trong audio, người nói đề cập rằng học kỳ trước ( last term ) là basketball , nhưng kỳ này ( now ) là swimming . Từ đó ta biết chắc chắn môn thể thao của kỳ hiện tại là swimming . ✅ Đáp án đúng : swimming 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ basketball => Môn này diễn ra ở kỳ trước (last term), không phải kỳ hiện tại. Nếu không chú ý kỹ, học viên dễ chọn nhầm đáp án này.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: swimming

Như vậy, đáp án chính xác là nhạc cụ piano . ✅ Đáp án đúng : piano 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ flute hoặc clarinet => Đây là các nhạc cụ được nhắc đến vào các ngày thứ Hai và thứ Năm, không phải thứ Ba, nếu không nghe kỹ ngày học viên có thể chọn sai.

Người đàn ông đồng ý với đề xuất mới này, vì vậy đáp án chính xác là thời gian mà người mẹ đã chọn: 10.15 . ✅ Đáp án đúng : 10.15 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ 9.30 => Người đàn ông có đề nghị thời gian 9.30, nhưng người mẹ không đồng ý vì bận đi nha sĩ, nên đáp án này sẽ không đúng nhé. ❌ 9.40 => Thời gian 9.40 là thời gian mẹ hẹn nha sĩ, không phải thời gian gặp hiệu trưởng, nên đáp án này sai nhé.

passages.title: Proposed changes
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Proposed changes"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:46] AUDIO: Welcome everyone. Thanks for coming to this information evening. The purpose of this meeting is to give you a chance to learn more about the road and rail improvement project. We've identified several problem areas and we've come up with some changes that we think will improve the local environment.

[01:04] AUDIO: For the shared access paths, by those I mean the paths shared by both bikes and pedestrians, we plan to turn these into open areas with grass around them. Cyclists and pedestrians need to be able to see each other clearly to avoid any accidents. So we've decided to remove the large native trees from the area for that reason. Now along the highway we want to put trees that are native to this area to add shade and make it more attractive.

[01:33] AUDIO: We thought possibly the spotted gum which grows naturally here. Now I know those of you who live in the housing estate are disturbed by the sound of traffic nearby. We are aiming to solve this problem by constructing a wall between the estate and the road and possibly in the future we might consider adding some artwork to it. We think this will be quite an effective solution.

[01:55] AUDIO: Moving on now to the local roads we want to encourage more public transport use and solve some of our traffic problems. So we're going to add a considerable number of stops to the bus routes that run along those roads. Just finally as a way of thanking the community for their cooperation we plan to make the picnic area in the park near the bus terminal more attractive. So we're adding some colourful new rose beds that gardeners will be putting in at the completion of the project.

[02:25] AUDIO: Before you hear the rest of the talk you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20. Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20. Now I'd like to give you more information about the renovations to Richlands train station. Can you all see a copy of the plan?

[03:13] AUDIO: We envisage Richlands station as more than just a train station. It'll be a transport hub linking all forms of transport in the area. To this end we're building an underground park and ride car park so commuters can drive to the station, park and then ride to work on the train. That's the entrance to it on the corner of Progress and Garden Road.

[03:37] AUDIO: You can drive into it from Progress Road. Now on the Progress Road side of the site on the top left of your map is where we plan to put the bus interchange. Commuters will have direct access to the platform from the bus interchange via a covered walkway. Cycling is an important part of our city's transport plan so cyclists will also be fully catered for with 80 new bicycle lockers.

[04:04] AUDIO: You can see where they are on the plan in the bottom left hand corner next to the bike path. Cyclists can ride to the station, store their bikes in the lockers and board the train. Oh and I forgot the most important thing. You'll even be able to shower at the station after your bike ride as we're installing showers between the toilets and the platform.

[04:25] AUDIO: We'll also install a fountain at the station to make the area more attractive. You can see it in the centre of the plan and between the fountain and the ticket machine we're putting in a lift for our elderly and disabled passengers. They will be able to buy their ticket then pass directly to the platform via the lift. So I hope that gives you a much better idea of the new facilities that will be available at Richlands station.
[04:52] AUDIO: Now we would like your feedback about the project so...

passages.title: Climate change and allergies
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Climate change and allergies"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [01:04] Elliot: Have you had a chance to look at the information for our project yet, Beth?
[01:08] Beth: I've had a look at most of the stuff on the relationship between climate change and allergies and at the role played by pollen from flowering plants and trees.

[01:19] Elliot: Yeah, me too. The main message is that seasonal allergies seem to be getting worse. In just the last 20 years, the amount of pollen that's produced by the flowers on birch trees has tripled, and one in four people suffers from either hay fever or asthma, which is triggered by pollen.

[01:40] Beth: I read something about allergy sufferers being more likely to have a vitamin D deficiency because we no longer take cod liver oil as a vitamin supplement, like many people used to do in the 1950s in Britain. And since then, allergies have quadrupled in most European countries, but it was only in Britain that cod liver oil was so popular, so that argument doesn't really make sense.
[02:07] Elliot: No, it doesn't seem that relevant.
[02:10] Beth: What seems to be happening now is that an increasing number of people are getting their first attack in their 40s and 50s.
[02:17] Elliot: That must be because of the link with climate change causing rising temperatures. But CO2 levels are seriously affecting pollen counts too.
[02:27] Beth: As much as milder winters?
[02:29] Elliot: Definitely. CO2 helps stimulate plant growth, and several recent studies have shown that when plants are exposed to more CO2, they produce more pollen.
[02:41] Beth: Really? So people might experience more severe allergic symptoms in future?
[02:47] Elliot: That's right.
[02:48] Beth: And another factor is that the pollen season is changing.
[02:51] Elliot: Yes. Scientists are predicting spring will come five weeks earlier, by 2130.
[02:59] Beth: That's in the long term. But that doesn't mean that spring will come earlier every year. Look at last winter. That was really cold until March, and the pollen season was delayed.
[03:11] Beth: Whereas this year, spring came earlier and lasted longer.
[03:15] Elliot: Right. And another thing we should mention is ragweed.
[03:19] Beth: As an example of a plant species moving into new areas as a result of climate change.

[03:26] Elliot: Yes. In the US, it's already the major allergen, affecting millions of people in August and September. But we're starting to see it grow in Europe for the first time, which is really worrying because it's so allergenic.
[03:42] Beth: The problem with tree pollen is also worse in cities because there are so many hard surfaces around, and the pollen doesn't get absorbed so much, just stays in the air.
[03:53] Elliot: Yeah. Wasn't the pollen shown to be three times higher in one city?

[03:57] Beth: I think so. So because of this, many cities have started to ban the planting of certain types of trees. So shall we look at the different data tables for seasonal changes for pollen in Europe?
[04:53] Elliot: OK. But I think we should just focus on the trees and plants, which we have the most data for. So that's oak trees and birch trees and grass.
[05:04] Beth: Yes, that makes it more manageable. Shall we go through the data for each country in detail and pick out anything interesting?
[05:13] Elliot: All right. So, starting with Austria. Well, here we've only got data for birch pollen. I wonder why there's no data for oak or grass?
[05:25] Beth: It would be interesting to compare with neighbouring countries.
[05:29] Elliot: True.
[05:30] Beth: The picture in France is unusual.

[05:33] Elliot: Yes, the pollen season starts earlier for both oak and birch, but it doesn't start any earlier for grass. I wonder why that is? In the Netherlands, we've got complete data for all three plants.

[05:48] Beth: So what does it show? Grass and birch pollen are only starting a few days earlier, but oak pollen is starting much earlier, 18 days in fact. That's unusual. There's not such a big difference in other countries.
[06:06] Elliot: No. Switzerland's an interesting case. The pollen season starts here earlier than in the past for oak, birch and grass.
[06:15] Beth: Yeah, from 21 days to 14 days earlier.
[06:19] Elliot: Yeah. The UK shows a different picture again.
[06:23] Beth: Yeah. Here the problem is that wet summers have extended the grass pollen season from five weeks to eight weeks, which is bad news for allergy sufferers.
[06:34] Elliot: Right. Well, I think we should have another look...

options: because people's diets have improved since the 1950s
because most people get enough vitamin D
because the evidence only applies in Britain

And since then, allergies have quadrupled in most European countries, but it was only in Britain that cod liver oil was so popular, so that argument doesn't really make sense. No, it doesn't seem that relevant."
