Từ khóa ở đây là: "vitamin D deficiency", "unconvinced", "Britain". bạn cần tập trung nghe phần thông tin nói về mối quan hệ giữa vitamin D và allergies.) ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : "I read something about allergy sufferers being more likely to have a vitamin D deficiency..." ☺️ Giải thích : Beth có đề cập đến một giả thuyết rằng việc thiếu vitamin D (vitamin D deficiency) liên quan đến tăng tỷ lệ dị ứng. Cô nói trong những năm 1950 tại Anh, người ta thường uống dầu gan cá (cod liver oil) – một nguồn cung cấp vitamin D tốt. Nhưng cô nhận ra từ đó đến nay, dị ứng đã tăng gấp bốn lần ở nhiều nước Châu Âu (quadruple
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: because the evidence only applies in Britain

questions.prompt: Eliot explains that rising CO2 levels
options: will mean distribution of pollen over a wider area.
are having less impact on pollen than milder winters.
are responsible for higher quantities of pollen.
questions.correct: are responsible for higher quantities of pollen.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "But CO2 levels are seriously affecting pollen counts too. As much as milder winters? Definitely. CO2 helps stimulate plant growth, and several recent studies have shown that when plants are exposed to more CO2, they produce more pollen."
explanation.step3: Elliot giải thích điều gì về sự gia tăng lượng khí CO₂ trong không khí? → (Tất cả đáp án đều liên quan đến tác động của khí CO₂ với lượng phấn hoa. bạn cần tập trung vào thông tin chính xác về tác động của CO₂ đối với phấn hoa.) ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : "CO2 levels are seriously affecting pollen counts too." ☺️ Giải thích : Elliot nói rõ rằng lượng CO₂ trong không khí đang gây ảnh hưởng nghiêm trọng đến lượng phấn hoa ( seriously affecting pollen counts ). Tiếp theo Elliot khẳng định rằng khí CO₂ giúp kích thích cây phát triển ( stimulate plant growth ) và các nghiên cứu gần đây cho thấy khi thực vật tiếp xúc nhiều hơn với CO₂, chúng sẽ tạo ra nhiều phấn hoa hơn ( produce more pollen ). Từ đây ta có thể suy luận rõ ràng, khí CO₂ tăng cao làm cho
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: are responsible for higher quantities of pollen.

questions.prompt: What does Beth say about seasonal changes?
options: There is no clear short-term trend for the arrival of spring.
In general, spring is likely to continue arriving early.
Springs are becoming milder and longer.
questions.correct: There is no clear short-term trend for the arrival of spring.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Scientists are predicting spring will come five weeks earlier, by 2130. That's in the long term. But that doesn't mean that spring will come earlier every year."
explanation.step3: Beth nói gì về sự thay đổi của các mùa trong năm? → (Câu hỏi yêu cầu hiểu về nhận định của Beth đối với các xu hướng thay đổi mùa. Từ khóa "seasonal changes" và "spring" là quan trọng nhất để tập trung nghe.) ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : "Scientists are predicting spring will come five weeks earlier..." ☺️ Giải thích : Elliot đề cập dự đoán dài hạn rằng mùa xuân sẽ đến sớm hơn 5 tuần vào năm 2130. Tuy nhiên, Beth đã phản bác ( But that doesn't mean spring will come earlier every year ), cho rằng không có xu hướng rõ ràng trong ngắn hạn. Beth dẫn chứng rằng mùa đông năm trước rất lạnh cho tới tháng Ba, khiến mùa phấn hoa bị trì hoãn, trong khi năm nay thì mùa xuân đến sớm hơn và kéo dài hơn. Từ đây có thể hiểu rằng, Beth đang chỉ ra không có xu hướng
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: There is no clear short-term trend for the arrival of spring.

questions.prompt: What point is made about the plant ragweed?
options: It is spreading to more countries.
It is the most widespread cause of allergies globally.
It causes the most severe type of allergy.
questions.correct: It is spreading to more countries.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And another thing we should mention is ragweed. As an example of a plant species moving into new areas as a result of climate change. Yes. In the US, it's already the major allergen, affecting millions of people in August and September. But we're starting to see it grow in Europe for the first time, which is really worrying because it's so allergenic."
explanation.step3: Điều gì được nói về cây ragweed ? → (Từ khóa chính là ragweed – một loại cây gây dị ứng. Mình cần nghe xem ragweed đang lan rộng , có phải nguyên nhân phổ biến nhất gây dị ứng , hay gây dị ứng nặng nhất .) ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : "And another thing we should mention is ragweed..." ☺️ Giải thích : Elliot nói rằng ragweed is already the major allergen in the US , ảnh hưởng đến hàng triệu người. Sau đó, Beth bổ sung rằng we’re starting to see it grow in Europe for the first time . Điều này cho thấy ragweed đang lan sang các khu vực mới , cụ thể là châu Âu , chứ không chỉ còn ở Mỹ nữa. ✅ Đáp án đúng: A – It is spreading to more countries. 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ B – “It is the most widespread cause of allergies globally”: Ragweed được nói là gây dị
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: It is spreading to more countries.

questions.prompt: Why is tree pollen a more serious problem in cities?
options: There is less to absorb the tree pollen.
There is not enough control over tree-planting.
questions.correct: There is less to absorb the tree pollen.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The problem with tree pollen is also worse in cities because there are so many hard surfaces around, and the pollen doesn't get absorbed so much, just stays in the air."
explanation.step3: Tại sao phấn hoa từ cây là vấn đề nghiêm trọng hơn ở thành phố? → (Từ khóa chính ở đây là tree pollen và in cities – mình cần nghe lý do tại sao phấn hoa từ cây lại gây vấn đề hơn ở đô thị so với nông thôn.) ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : "The problem with tree pollen is also worse in cities..." ☺️ Giải thích : Beth nói: "There are so many hard surfaces around, and the pollen doesn't get absorbed so much, just stays in the air." Ý nghĩa là do bề mặt cứng như bê tông, đường nhựa... nên phấn hoa không được hấp thụ , và bay lơ lửng trong không khí lâu hơn . ✅ Đáp án đúng: B – There is less to absorb the tree pollen 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ A – “Trees produce more pollen there”: Không có thông tin nói rằng cây trong thành phố sản xuất nhiều phấn hoa hơn. ❌
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: There is less to absorb the tree pollen.

explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The picture in France is unusual. Yes, the pollen season starts earlier for both oak and birch, but it doesn't start any earlier for grass."
explanation.step3: Tình hình mùa phấn hoa ở France (Pháp) như thế nào? → Mình cần chú ý xem có bao nhiêu loại phấn hoa được nhắc đến và có sự thay đổi gì ở thời điểm bắt đầu mùa phấn. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : “The picture in France is unusual.” ☺️ Giải thích : Elliot nói: “The pollen season starts earlier for both oak and birch, but it doesn't start any earlier for grass.” Vậy là có sự thay đổi với 2 loại phấn hoa: oak và birch , còn grass thì không có thay đổi . ✅ Đáp án đúng: B – changes identified for two pollen types only 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ D – earlier start dates for all pollen types => Grass pollen không thay đổi, nên câu này sai. ❌ A – greatest change recorded for oak pollen => Không có so sánh về mức độ thay đổi, chỉ nói là mùa bắt đầu sớm hơn. ❌ G –
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: changes identified for two pollen types only

Trong các lựa chọn, chỉ có một đáp án nói rõ về sự thay đổi đáng kể của oak pollen . ✅ Đáp án đúng: A – greatest change recorded for oak pollen 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ F – little difference in start dates => K

passages.title: Textiles with Business Studies
content: 📌 Textiles with Business Studies
New development
• Now possible to work with the [ _____ ] Faculty to widen learning opportunities
Aims of course
• To cover three areas of textiles: - knitted
- woven
• To focus on related business operations
• Work placement: focus on studio work in the context of the [ _____ ]
Course content
Year One: experimentation
Visual research with [ _____ ] and suggestions for its application
Year Two: relating skills to the real world
Optional course: [ _____ ] design processes
Three- or four-year course? Students are offered [ _____ ] to help them make their decision.
Year Three: consolidation
Learning style: [ _____ ] practice
Students produce:
- a dissertation
- a portfolio
Career opportunities
Within textile business- e.g. stylists, retail managers
Further opportunities-jobs in [ _____ ] and trend forecasting
If interested - come back tomorrow for a short [ _____ ]
transcript: [01:16] AUDIO: Thank you first of all for coming along to the University's Open Day and in particular for coming to this talk to find out about our course in textiles with business studies. The cooperation between the Faculty of Arts and Architecture and the business faculty enables us to offer this undergraduate and integrated master's course. In the five years this course has been running, we've learned a lot and it's become very popular. Now, thanks to the Faculty of Engineering, we're also able to offer a really exciting opportunity to those who would like to further diversify and would like to carry their learning through into new disciplines.

[01:58] AUDIO: Now, the aims of this course are firstly to create innovative and highly motivated textile practitioners within the disciplines of knitted textiles, an increasingly popular area, as you will have seen on the catwalks, printed and of course woven textiles. Secondly, we also ensure that our students gain an in-depth knowledge and understanding of related business operations. We make sure that our students have sufficient hands-on experience by arranging interesting and relevant work placements. The focus of the integrated component of the work placement is the global market.

[02:39] AUDIO: Our aim is to locate studio work in this increasingly important context. Moving on to what we do in each year. In the first year students explore the three subject areas of textiles in rotation. The emphasis for the first year is experimentation and we ask for evidence of visual research which must be supported by documentation and proposals for its application.

[03:07] AUDIO: In year two design and technical skills are related to the real world. Unlike many other university textile courses these days, we give our students the opportunity to choose an extra module on the traditional processes of design which gives a historical perspective on their work. This can be done before introducing students to computer aided design. Students at this point, year two, decide if they intend to complete the course at year three with a BA ons or progress to year four and conclude with a master's in design.

[03:46] AUDIO: Students can also have tutorials if they feel they need help making this important decision. This reflects our commitment to student support at all times. Year three consolidates the knowledge gained using a particular learning style. It's called reflective practice.

[04:09] AUDIO: That means you look back on what you've done and analyse and evaluate your subject in both academic and professional contexts. This helps and encourages deeper understanding. Students produce a dissertation on a topic of their own choosing and a portfolio of their textile collection. Also to help underpin the commercial aspect of the course we ask for a business plan.

[04:36] AUDIO: On the subject of career opportunities many graduates work directly within the textile business with careers commonly found as stylists and retail managers. However it shouldn't be forgotten that there are many other exciting opportunities out there. For example careers in journalism for those with a flair for words or trend forecasting for those with their eye on the we are certain that we shall see broader and more varied opportunities for our graduates. If you like what you've heard today and are thinking of applying for the program and you'd like to talk to us further please come back tomorrow.

[05:18] AUDIO: You'll have the opportunity to do a brief interview where we'll be able to assess your aptitude for this subject area. Many students who haven't studied related subjects may be surprised to find that they're quite well suited to our program. After that of course you'll need to go through the usual application procedures.

questions.prompt: • Now possible to work with the _____ Faculty to widen learning opportunities

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Now, thanks to the Faculty of Engineering, we're also able to offer a really exciting opportunity to those who would like to further diversify and would like to carry their learning through into new disciplines."
explanation.step3: “Now, thanks to the Faculty of Engineering, we’re also able to offer a really exciting opportunity…” → Vậy tên của faculty được nhắc đến là Engineering ✅ Đáp án đúng: Engineering 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ Business => Đã có business faculty trước đó, nhưng câu hỏi 31 đang nói đến một phát triển mới , không phải thông tin cũ. ❌ Arts => Faculty of Arts được nói tới ở phần đầu, nhưng cũng không liên quan đến new development ở câu hỏi này.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: engineering

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Now, the aims of this course are firstly to create innovative and highly motivated textile practitioners within the disciplines of knitted textiles, an increasingly popular area, as you will have seen on the catwalks, printed and of course woven textiles."
explanation.step3: ” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Đề bài liệt kê: knitted, …, woven → Như vậy chỗ trống cần điền là tên loại textile còn thiếu giữa “knitted” và “woven” Trong bài nghe, ta nghe được ba loại: “… knitted textiles, an increasingly popular area, as you will have seen on the catwalks, printed and of course woven textiles.” → Loại ở giữa là printed ✅ Đáp án đúng: printed 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ dyed => Không được nhắc tới trong audio ❌ woven => Đã được liệt kê ở cuối danh sách rồi, không phải là loại cần điền ở giữa
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: printed

questions.prompt: • Work placement: focus on studio work in the context of the _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The focus of the integrated component of the work placement is the global market."
explanation.step3: ” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Đề bài nói rằng work placement sẽ tập trung vào một “context” cụ thể → Ta cần xác định ngữ cảnh mà studio work được đặt vào Trong audio, ta nghe được: “…The focus of the integrated component of the work placement is the global market.” → Nghĩa là studio work sẽ được đặt trong bối cảnh thị trường toàn cầu ✅ Đáp án đúng: global market 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ international business => Gần nghĩa nhưng không chính xác với từ dùng trong audio ❌ workplace => Không đủ thông tin, không phản ánh đúng cụm “global market” trong audio
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: global market

questions.prompt: Visual research with _____ and suggestions for its application

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The emphasis for the first year is experimentation and we ask for evidence of visual research which must be supported by documentation and proposals for its application."
explanation.step3: “...we ask for evidence of visual research which must be supported by documentation and proposals for its application.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi yêu cầu ta điền visual research with ____ and suggestions for its application Trong audio, ta nghe thấy: “...evidence of visual research which must be supported by documentation and proposals...” → Vậy từ cần điền là từ documentation , tức là “tài liệu minh chứng cho quá trình nghiên cứu trực quan” ✅ Đáp án đúng: documentation 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ evidence => “Evidence” được đề cập nhưng là yêu cầu tổng quát , không phải từ cần điền ở đây. ❌ proposals => Đây là phần bổ sung cho documentation chứ không phải đứng riêng.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: documentation

questions.prompt: Optional course: _____ design processes

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Unlike many other university textile courses these days, we give our students the opportunity to choose an extra module on the traditional processes of design which gives a historical perspective on their work."
explanation.step3: “...choose an extra module on the traditional processes of design which gives a historical perspective...” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi yêu cầu ta điền: Optional course: ______ design processes Trong bài nghe, người nói đề cập: “...an extra module on the traditional processes of design...” → Vậy từ cần điền là traditional , tạo thành cụm “traditional design processes” ✅ Đáp án đúng: traditional 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ historical => Mặc dù “historical perspective” được nhắc tới, nhưng “historical” không mô tả “design processes” mà là “perspective”. ❌ computer-aided => Đây là phần sau được giới thiệu, không phải phần optional course như đề hỏi.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: traditional

questions.prompt: Three- or four-year course? Students are offered _____ to help them make their decision.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Students can also have tutorials if they feel they need help making this important decision."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Students can also have tutorials if they feel they need help making this important decision.” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi là: Students are offered ______ to help them make their decision. Trong bài nghe, chúng ta nghe thấy: “Students can also have tutorials if they feel they need help...” → Từ “tutorials” được dùng chính xác để nói về hỗ trợ ra quyết định → phù hợp với chỗ cần điền. ✅ Đáp án đúng: tutorials 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ support => support là ý khái quát, không phải là cụ thể hình thức hỗ trợ như đề hỏi. ❌ interviews => Interviews chỉ được nhắc ở phần cuối khi nói về buổi gặp mặt – không liên quan đến quyết định giữa 3 năm và 4 năm học.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: tutorials

questions.prompt: Learning style: _____ practice

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Year three consolidates the knowledge gained using a particular learning style. It's called reflective practice."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Year three consolidates the knowledge gained using a particular learning style. It’s called reflective practice .” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Câu hỏi yêu cầu: Learning style: ______ practice Trong đoạn nghe, cụm từ “ reflective practice ” được nhấn mạnh rõ ràng là phương pháp học ở năm 3 → trùng khớp chính xác với câu hỏi. ✅ Đáp án đúng: reflective 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ practical => practical practice nghe có vẻ hợp lý nhưng không được nhắc trong đoạn này. ❌ academic => academic practice là một dạng học tập nhưng không phải là kiểu mà đề bài đang hỏi tới.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: reflective

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Students produce a dissertation on a topic of their own choosing and a portfolio of their textile collection. Also to help underpin the commercial aspect of the course we ask for a business plan."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “Students produce a dissertation on a topic of their own choosing and a portfolio of their textile collection. Also to help underpin the commercial aspect of the course we ask for a business plan .” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Trong danh sách, ngoài “dissertation” và “portfolio”, đề bài hỏi thêm một sản phẩm nữa. Ngay sau khi đề cập đến hai mục trên, người nói nói thêm “we ask for a business plan” → đây là tài liệu thứ ba mà sinh viên phải nộp. ✅ Đáp án đúng: business plan 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ project => project là từ hay xuất hiện trong đề tài sinh viên nhưng không được nói tới trong phần này. ❌ proposal => proposal thường dùng ở các năm đầu hoặc cho nghiên cứu, không phải ở năm 3 khi đã có dissertation.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: business plan

questions.prompt: Further opportunities-jobs in _____ and trend forecasting

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "For example careers in journalism for those with a flair for words or trend forecasting for those with their eye on the we are certain that we shall see broader and more varied opportunities for our graduates."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “For example careers in journalism for those with a flair for words or trend forecasting for those with their eye on…” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Sau khi nói về các công việc trong ngành dệt may như stylist và retail manager, người nói liệt kê các cơ hội nghề nghiệp khác . Một trong các nghề được nhắc đầu tiên là journalism – nghề báo chí, phù hợp với người có khả năng viết tốt. Đây chính là từ cần điền vì nó là lĩnh vực nằm ngoài “textile business”. ✅ Đáp án đúng: journalism 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ media => media là một ngành liên quan nhưng không được nhắc đến cụ thể trong audio. ❌ communication => từ này không được đề cập, và cũng quá chung chung.
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: journalism

questions.prompt: If interested - come back tomorrow for a short _____

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "If you like what you've heard today and are thinking of applying for the program and you'd like to talk to us further please come back tomorrow. You'll have the opportunity to do a brief interview where we'll be able to assess your aptitude for this subject area."
explanation.step3: ▶️ Thông tin cần nghe ở : “If you like what you've heard today and are thinking of applying for the program and you'd like to talk to us further please come back tomorrow. You'll have the opportunity to do a brief interview ...” ☺️ Cùng xem giải thích nhé : Từ khóa “come back tomorrow” giúp ta xác định đúng đoạn cần nghe. Người nói tiếp tục giải thích rằng học sinh sẽ có cơ hội tham gia một brief interview (cuộc phỏng vấn ngắn). Đây là đáp án cần điền vì đề hỏi: “If interested - come back tomorrow for a short…?” và từ phù hợp nhất là “interview”. ✅ Đáp án đúng: interview 🧐 Lưu ý bẫy đề thi : ❌ meeting => meeting là một cuộc gặp gỡ chung chung, không đúng mục đích “đánh giá năng lực” của từ “interview”. ❌ discussion => discussion mang nghĩa
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: interview

transcript: [00:00] Julie: Hello. Could I speak to Mr. John Girdlestone, please?
[00:04] John: Speaking.
[00:05] Julie: Oh, hi. My name is Julie Bloom. I'm studying here in the UK for a year, and a friend told me you organise an international club where people of different nationalities can meet up?
[00:19] John: That's right. The club was founded over 50 years ago, and at present we've got members from approximately 30 countries. What's the name of your friend?
[00:31] Julie: Louise. She's back in the States now.
[00:33] John: Oh, Louise. I remember her. So, are you from the States too, Julie?
[00:39] Julie: Yes, from California.
[00:41] John: Great. Well, let's see what I can tell you about the club. It doesn't cost a lot to become a member. You can join for two months for £2.50, or it's £8.50 for 12 months.
[00:54] Julie: And is it only for university students?
[00:58] John: No, we're open to anyone. We have quite a few members from the language schools in town, and also local people who are interested in meeting people from other countries.
[01:09] Julie: OK. So, what sorts of things do you do?
[01:13] John: Well, one thing we organize on a regular basis is dancing. That's a great way to get to know people.
[01:20] Julie: Do you mean like disco?

[01:21] John: No, we don't do disco. We do folk dances, some from Europe, but some from further afield. Everyone really enjoys them. We meet on Monday evenings at 8.30. Do you know the University Centre?
[01:38] Julie: Yes, I think so.
[01:40] John: We meet there, in the main hall. Don't get confused with the old hall, where there's a ballroom dancing group. They're nothing to do with us.
[01:50] Julie: And can I just show up?
[01:52] John: Sure, everyone's welcome. And do I need to come along with a partner for the dancing? You don't have to, though you can if you want to. I'm sure you'll have a good time.
[02:04] John: We have live music for some sessions. I don't suppose you play a musical instrument, do you?
[02:11] Julie: I play the violin, but I'm not very good.
[02:14] John: Well, we're looking for some people to join the band. If you're interested, why don't you call Mike? His number's 01356 890674.
[02:29] Julie: OK, thanks.
[02:31] John: Then we also have a meal together regularly. That's once a month, and it's always on a Sunday, the second one of the month.
[02:40] Julie: Oh, so that'll be this coming Sunday. And where's that held?

[02:45] John: In the university centre again, in the canteen. We used to have it in the restaurant on the ground floor, but that's closed at weekends now, unfortunately, so we're up on the top floor. They do very reasonably priced meals, things like baked potatoes and pizza.
[03:05] Julie: And can I just show up there?

[03:07] John: Absolutely. Then we have some special summer events too. On July the 2nd, we're going to a place called Great Hampton, about half an hour's drive away, to take part in the carnival they hold there every year. It's always a good day out, especially if it's a sunny day.
[03:44] Julie: Oh, Louise said she went on that last year. She said it was really good, and it'd be nice to go somewhere out of town.
[03:53] John: Well, in that case, you might be interested in our event on July the 16th. That's a walk in the Stannard Hills. We do about 15 kilometres, so it's a decent walk, and it's for charity.
[04:08] Julie: Sounds a pretty long way.
[04:10] John: Then on August the 7th, we're having a garden party at the home of one of our organisers. She has an outdoor pool, so if the weather's warm enough, you'll be able to go swimming.
[04:22] Julie: OK. Hard to imagine that today.

[04:26] John: Well, the summer hasn't really started yet. Then our last summer events on September the 4th. Last year, we went to a castle, but this year, we're going to the theatre. We do ask members to let us know in advance for that, so we can book.
[04:43] Julie: Sure. Well, I'd definitely like to join.

passages.title: A museum site
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "A museum site"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:31] AUDIO: Welcome to Brampton Museum. I'm going to tell you a little bit about the museum first, and then show you around. As you can see, Brampton is an open-air museum. The first open-air museums were established in Scandinavia towards the end of the 19th century, and the concept soon spread throughout Europe and North America, and there are several in Britain, all of which tell the history of a particular part of the country.

[01:03] AUDIO: Brampton focuses on life during the 19th century. The site was chosen because there were already some historic 19th century buildings here, and others have been dismantled in different parts of the region and rebuilt on the site. This hadn't been attempted before in these parts, so we're very proud of what we have here. All of the buildings are filled with furniture, machinery and objects.

[01:32] AUDIO: You may be able to see these in other museums, but not in their original settings. What also sets Brampton apart from other museums is that the story of the exhibits is told not by labels, but by costumed staff like myself. I look after sheep, cows and hens, which are much the same as those you see on modern farms, but I use traditional methods to care for them. You will also be able to see a blacksmith and a printer, as well as other craftspeople.

[02:08] AUDIO: If you talk to them, you'll be able to find out what life was really like 150 years ago. Our programme of activities during the year has guided walks, an agricultural fair and all the other events you would expect a museum to have, but remember, here you experience them in the real surroundings. The site is divided into different areas. The main building contains our high street, which is a street of 19th century shops, offices and some homes.

[02:44] AUDIO: There's a stationer's shop, which sells a range of specially selected cards, prints and copies of Victorian stationery, all available for purchase by visitors. Upstairs in the same building, a printer demonstrates the production of posters, business cards and advertising material. Across the street from the stationers is a clothes shop and there's a baker's where you can watch a demonstration of someone making bread, cakes and pastries. We also have a sweet shop, which has old-fashioned sweets for sale.

[03:24] AUDIO: Vintage trams travel along from one end of the street to the other, carrying visitors on their journey into the past. We will also be visiting the farm and taking a ride on a steam train. Of course, the main form of transport in those days was the horse, and you can watch horses being exercised in the old stables. This part of Britain was famous for coal mining, and on the site we have part of a mine which opened in 1860 and was worked for over a hundred years, before closing in 1963.

[04:03] AUDIO: Visitors can put on a hard hat and take a guided tour underground to see how coal was worked and to experience the working conditions in the early 1900s. Now, if you'd like to look at your map, we'll begin our tour. The site is a bit like a circle with the railway going around the edge. You can see where we are now by the entrance, and we're going to start by walking to the high street.

[04:59] AUDIO: We'll go to the crossroads in the middle of the map and go straight on, making our way between two buildings on either side of the path. The larger one is an exhibition centre, but it's not open today, unfortunately. The other building is offices. The path leads directly to the high street building, which is at the opposite side of the site to the entrance.

[05:25] AUDIO: Here you're free to wander around and take a ride up and down on a tram. We'll then take the path which follows the railway line and crosses it to the farm. If you wish, you can have tea in the farmhouse, and there'll be time to look at the animals and the machinery. Then we cross the railway line again and visit our special attraction, which is the coal mine.

[05:52] AUDIO: It's just in front of us here at the entrance. We'll return to the crossroads and walk through a small wooded area to the manor house. This is one of the original buildings on the site and belonged to a wealthy farmer. You can look around the house and gardens and talk to our guides who can tell you what it was like to live there.

[06:16] AUDIO: We will then follow a path which goes past the pond and will take us to the railway station, which is situated between the path and the railway line. Finally, we'll take the steam train back around the site, passing alongside the high street and the coal mine back to the entrance. So, if you'd like to follow me...

questions.prompt: Which TWO things make the museum unusual? (Answer 1 of 2)

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "What also sets Brampton apart from other museums is that the story of the exhibits is told not by labels, but by costumed staff like myself."
explanation.step3: Which TWO things make the museum unusual? → Câu hỏi yêu cầu mình chọn hai yếu tố đặc biệt khiến bảo tàng này khác biệt so với những bảo tàng khác . ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Từ đoạn “What also sets Brampton apart from other museums…” (00:01:38 → 00:02:00) ☺️ Giải thích : Elliot nói: “What also sets Brampton apart from other museums is that the story of the exhibits is told not by labels, but by costumed staff like myself.” → Điều đặc biệt là hướng dẫn viên mặc trang phục thời xưa và kể chuyện chứ không dùng bảng thông tin → A. the guides là đúng. passages.title: Professor's Lecture
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Professor's Lecture"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:53] Jim: Jane, what did you think of Professor Morgan's lecture? I don't know about you, but I find it incredibly difficult to believe that light influences the environment as much as he says. I've never seen any journal articles, websites or anything that verifies his arguments. It's stupid.

[01:15] Jane: On the contrary, I've seen a great deal of research supporting his argument from a wide range of renowned scientists. Have you looked at the recommended textbook listed on the course outline given to us at the beginning of the semester? All the information is in there. Perhaps you've just been looking in the wrong places.

[01:35] Jim: I never look at the course outlines. I have so many loose sheets of paper I tend to lose anything I'm given by the end of the day. What's the textbook they recommend, and where can I get it from? I should probably go buy it soon.
[01:50] Jim: I'm already behind in the course.

[01:53] Jane: Yeah, you definitely should buy it, and our grades are more important this year. It's called The Influence of Light on the Environment. You should be able to find it in the bookshop on campus. If not, they'll order it within two weeks.
[02:10] Jane: In the meantime, you should read up on Ken Simpson's work. He argues that in order to protect natural habitats, governments should endeavour to turn off lights in cities at night.

[02:23] Jim: Well, that's controversial. I doubt any government would be willing to do that any time soon. I imagine roads would become quite dangerous without street lighting. For this issue, Dave Kepler suggests they could just replace the existing lights with more environmentally friendly bulbs.

[02:44] Jim: They could even install solar-powered lights. That way, roads will be more eco-friendly while maintaining safety. Although I guess they wouldn't be particularly effective in colder countries, especially during the winter.

[02:59] Jane: That's quite a good idea, actually. The price of solar power is supposed to be on par with electricity within the next few decades, and it was on the news this morning. I've also heard that, according to Sharon Gray, in countries with more sunlight, insect-eating animals tend to be smaller in size, since there are fewer insects, and the remaining insects produced a smaller number of eggs.

[03:27] Jim: Yeah, I think I read somewhere that sunlight also has a negative effect on the quality of water, but I'm not sure I believe it. In many hot countries, particularly developing countries, there is a lot of water pollution caused by factories rather than sunlight. Nevertheless, Maria Jackson says that in direct sunlight, the surface of the water becomes more translucent. Therefore, it affects the amount of sunlight that aquatic insects can absorb.
[03:58] Jim: Not much research has been undertaken to prove Jackson's theory, but it seems to have been widely accepted anyway.

[04:06] Jane: I've never heard of that. I'll have to look it up on Google. The only other theory I've studied is Barbara Swallow's study on how declined insect population adversely affects the frog population. Not that I'm complaining.
[04:23] Jane: I hate insects, especially spiders.
[04:25] Jim: You have arachnophobia? I never would have guessed. Didn't your brother have a pet black widow spider?
[04:32] Jane: Yes, he did, and I hated it. It escaped from its cage once and we never found it. I had nightmares for months. OK, now I'm getting goosebumps.
[05:21] Jane: Let's change the subject. What's your stance on natural and artificial light?

[05:27] Jim: Honestly, I'm not sure it makes much difference which one you use. Species will die out either way. I think the real argument we should consider is global warming and protection or replacement of finite fuels. Solar power provides us with an incredible opportunity to replace electricity, and governments should definitely increase spending on research in this field.
[05:54] Jim: The theories discussed in our lectures, like Simpson's and Gray's, are so vague and lack proof, so I don't understand why we even study them.

[06:05] Jane: I see what you mean. I don't like learning unsupported theories for exams, and I'd rather spend my time learning something else. For example, I'd be much more interested in studying the animals in safari parks than researching migratory birds, particularly the effect of tourists on the quality of life of animals. As we know, every year thousands of visitors will drive in their own vehicles or ride in vehicles provided by the facility to observe freely roaming animals.

[06:38] Jim: Yeah, that would be really interesting, especially those animals living in more tropical countries like Borneo. Following on from that, I want to study how bringing animals over from foreign countries to put in our zoos affects their life expectancy. For example, do you remember when China sent pandas to Edinburgh Zoo? Apparently, one of the pandas became depressed, but it was never explained why.
[07:06] Jim: To me, obviously, you can't take an animal out of its natural habitat and put it in a cage on the other side of the world. It just doesn't work.

2500 years ago, in Peter Rochet's findings: Roman trading [ _____ ] for grains in Turenne.In the 1500s, a French found the remains of a [ _____ ]After that, British and Swedish archaeologists conducted a full [ _____ ] in this area.

transcript: [00:57] AUDIO: Okay, in this lecture we are going to learn the history of Turin, which is a county in southern part of France. We will also be looking at some archaeological findings as they are the basis of what we know today. The history of this area can date back to 2500 years ago. In the earliest years, there were just small settlements where people lived a very simple life.

[01:23] AUDIO: Slowly, the place grew into a town and became livelier and business activities began to emerge. According to Peter Rocher, a French archaeologist, this place was an important agricultural county since a long time ago. In his findings, there were buried pieces of grain and broken utensils which were the evidence of ancient Romans who traded their pottery for grains with people in Turin. This also proves that the business activities were quite active in this area back then.

[01:58] AUDIO: However, it is something else that gave us a much better idea of what life was like in Turin about 2000 years ago. In the 1500s, a Frenchman found what seemed to be the remains of a castle when he was digging a well. There were bricks and stones that looked like part of a building. In the 17th century, a group of British archaeologists came to Turin to study the relics.

[02:28] AUDIO: Later, Swedish government also sent a team of archaeologists. The two teams did a thorough survey of the whole area together. It was hard work which took them several months to dig out the ruins of old buildings and recover the area to what it originally looked like. The outcome of their work was surprising for all of them.

[02:54] AUDIO: It was a very big area of buildings and facilities for different purposes, which was a very good proof that a civilisation existed from so long ago. In the north-eastern part of the area, archaeologists found signs of a local market. There were stone stands that sellers used to place their commodities and they even found silver coins which were the currency back then. It further proved that the business was flourishing in ancient Turin.

[03:26] AUDIO: About one mile to the east, in the eastern part of that region, archaeologists found the remains of a building. From the words on a stone, they knew the building was called cast. It looked like an old workshop and archaeologists found tools for making textiles. It was a very important evidence that this industry was established about more than 2000 years ago, which was situated in the central area was a big round building where there was something like a fountain.

[03:58] AUDIO: The team found buckets near it. This showed that it had been the place where people collected water. We could imagine the scene that dozens of people were standing by this fountain with buckets in their hands. What surprised the archaeologists most was that there was an ancient theatre in the north-eastern part.

[04:21] AUDIO: There was a stage and several stone seats uncovered. Right next to the theatre, archaeologists unearthed a long stone. Then more stones were found and they extended across a deeper area. From this, we could conclude that these stones were from an old bridge on the river.

[04:42] AUDIO: Architects were very skilled back then. They used their wisdom to conquer technical obstacles, but people used their wisdom much more than Millie for practical purposes. In the south-western area, what seemed to be like a garden was uncovered. There were pots and wooden basins.

[05:02] AUDIO: It must have been a very beautiful place, full of plants and flowers of different colours. More importantly, there were two statues of lions just beside the gate. It means French people admired the power of this beast at that time, so that they used stones to make these statues. Not far from Dolby House, also in the central area, there was an elevated area, but its lower area in the centre.

[05:31] AUDIO: Through a lot of careful research, archaeologists came to the conclusion that this was a Roman bath. It's where rich people went to enjoy a comfortable and relaxing hot bath. Next to the bath, there was a sculpture of a woman who was like pouring water into the bath. Across from it, on the other side of the bath pool, people can see the sculpture of the Roman emperor who ruled this area for many years.
[05:59] AUDIO: These discoveries are good material for us to study the history of Turin and southern France. What we're going to do now is...

passages.title: Winsham Farm Centre
content: Address: Winsham Farm, [ _____ ] Road, near SherbornePostcode:[ _____ ]
transcript: [02:31] Woman: Hello, Winsham Farm Centre.
[02:34] Man: Oh, hello. I want to arrange a weekend away for myself and some people from work and we heard about your centre. I wonder if you could give me some details.
[02:44] Woman: Yes, certainly. We are a residential centre attached to a working farm and we organise educational activities for those guests who want them. Um, what else would you like to know?
[02:58] Man: Well, firstly, what kind of accommodation have you got?
[03:02] Woman: We've got eight rooms altogether and we can sleep thirty-eight at any one time. Three of the rooms have got six bunks and five of them have got four bunks.
[03:13] Man: Right. And what other facilities are there?

[03:16] Woman: We have separate toilets and showers for each of the rooms. There's a large dining room and a large meeting room which can be booked by groups in advance. But I'm afraid we had a flood in there last month and the floor was slightly damaged so unfortunately it's out of use just now. We've got workmen coming in next week.
[03:37] Woman: When were you thinking of staying?
[03:39] Man: In three weeks time, the 28th of September.
[03:43] Woman: Oh, it should be OK by then.
[03:45] Man: Oh, well, that's OK then. And what about food? Do you provide meals or is it self-catering?

[03:52] Woman: We're very flexible. As long as you give us enough notice, we can cater for you or, if you prefer, you can just bring your own food and use the kitchen facilities. And some people prefer to eat out, which is also fine.
[04:08] Man: Fine. And I heard that your farm is organic. Does that mean that you only have crops and no animals?

[04:15] Woman: It doesn't, actually. A lot of people seem to think that, but we do rear livestock as well. And so we have a wide range of food. Organic means it's all produced without the use of artificial fertilisers or pesticides.
[04:30] Man: I see. That sounds good. Could you tell me what sort of recreational activities are available, either at the centre or in the area?
[04:39] Woman: Yes. Here at the centre, we offer farm tours. They're very popular. One of the farm managers shows people around and explains some of the principles of organic farming.
[04:51] Woman: And for any visitors who are really keen, he'll let them drive a tractor or feed the animals and so on – with supervision, of course.
[05:00] Man: I think a lot of our group would be interested in that. It'd make a change from factory work.
[05:05] Woman: Well, if they fancy it, tell them to come prepared. Plenty of old clothing, especially footwear. It can be very messy and wet.
[05:14] Man: OK. I'll warn them.

[06:03] Woman: And another type of activity we do is survival courses, but that's only for groups of five or more. And they've got to be acquaintances. They have to co-operate closely. These courses are very popular, especially with school groups, but adults seem to enjoy them too.
[06:22] Man: What do they involve? Things like map reading?

[06:25] Woman: Well, not exactly. What it is, we've got a large area of woodland on the farm, and we run this course there. It's mainly about collecting food and water, lighting a fire without any equipment, that kind of thing.
[06:42] Man: This weekend could be hard work. What about the area around the centre? What is there to do?

[06:48] Woman: If you look at a map, you'll see that we're very well situated here. Our centre's about midway between the Exmoor National Park, which is very popular for hill-walking, and the South Coast, which has very good beaches.
[07:03] Man: Are they both within walking distance?

[07:05] Woman: Well, they're both a bit far, unless you're very fit, but they're only about 30 minutes by road. And there's also a cycle path, which starts quite near here, about 10 minutes' walk away. You can hire bikes at the starting point.
[07:20] Man: What is there to do if the weather's bad? I hope it won't be, but you never know.

[07:25] Woman: Yes, that's right. Well, on most Saturday evenings we show films here, and then once a month a group of local musicians performs in our meeting room. And then Sherbourne is only 14 miles away. It's only a small town, but it's got a very good museum and an old abbey, which is well worth a visit.
[07:44] Man: Well, it sounds perfect for our purposes. One last thing. What about prices? I'm not sure yet, but there'll probably be about 15 of us.

[07:55] Woman: We charge a standard £14 a head for accommodation, whether there are 10 or 20 of you or whatever, and about £7 for cooked meals, depending on the menu you want. Use of the kitchen facilities is extra, as is the hire of the meeting room. It depends, really, what exactly you want and for how many people.
[08:18] Man: Right. Well, I've made a note of all that, and I'll discuss it with the rest of the group. Then I'll get back to you with a firm booking. Can I do that by phone?
[08:27] Woman: Yes, you can. But once you've made a booking, we would need a deposit within five days to secure it. Then you just pay the balance when you're here.
[08:35] Man: Oh, yes, of course. Could you give me the address, please?
[08:40] Woman: Yes. It's Winsham Farm, Cotehele Road, that's C-O-T-E-H-E-L-E, near Sherbourne. And the postcode is S-H-12-1-L-Q.
[09:00] Man: Thank you.

passages.title: A theme park in Fun City
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "A theme park in Fun City"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [01:07] AUDIO: Welcome to our radio programme, Travel With Me. Today, I'll recommend you a fantastic place. It's the theme park in Fun City. It has been awarded the most popular tourist attraction in the city.

[01:22] AUDIO: So, just follow me to find something interesting there. The park opens at 9.30 every morning. For the first activity, I definitely advise you shouldn't miss the riding in the park. The actual riding begins at 10am, but I suggest you arrive a little earlier before the opening time, otherwise there might be a long wait.

[01:48] AUDIO: And how much, you may ask, does an entrance ticket cost? Well, there are two types of tickets, basic tickets and family fast line track tickets. You can either buy a ticket at the ticket office near the main entrance to the park, or reserve from the official website in advance. The latter is preferable, as it always offers a discount.

[02:12] AUDIO: For example, the original price for a basic ticket is £89, but if you buy it online, it only costs £78. For the family fast line track ticket, you only have to pay £95 on the internet, instead of its original price, £113. Visiting the lake in the park is also a good choice. There is a new refreshment room beside the lake, and the latest thing, it was only finished last month, is the splash ride.

[02:46] AUDIO: It is a new area and pretty exciting. Forget about wearing waterproofs, because you'll still get wet, and don't take cameras either. As a result, I strongly advise that the best time to visit the lake is in the hottest season, in case you catch a cold. Another activity you'll find exciting is riding the roller coaster bike.

[03:10] AUDIO: I suggest families with children go for a try, as it's always favoured by them. This roller coaster bike is different from the normal one, in that it's made of wood, so it's lighter. The person who designed it has won a special prize for innovation. For those who are not interested in these exciting activities, there is a resort for you.

[03:33] AUDIO: You can sit there talking, relaxing, or taking photos. Please remember, this section is for a picnic, so you have to prepare your own snacks. But don't worry about drinks, since free bottled water is available there. Oh, one more thing is, it's better to take a picnic blanket to sit on.

[03:54] AUDIO: After the picnic, if there is some time left, you can take part in some other interesting activities you like, such as watching the circus or going fishing. At the end of the one-day trip, there is a special event for you, the firework display. You'll enjoy a spectacular show in the sky. Everyone is cheering.

[04:16] AUDIO: I think it's a must for you, with a perfect ending of the day. OK, that was something about the most basic information, and now here's some more practical information about four popular activities on the brochure of the theme park, because some people want to know whether they're worth trying. Well, let's first look at the Cowboy Show. It's a dance show by a group of boys wearing cowboy boots and hats.

[05:24] AUDIO: What they perform tells the stories of cowboys' life. Rest assured that you don't need to queue for hours to get in, so please come and enjoy it. Then there is the driving school ride. In this activity, you can try a variety of vehicles, but please note that this one is only for those below 1.2 metres.

[05:47] AUDIO: The staff will measure your height at the entrance. Parents can just have a rest on the chair and watch their kids playing. You don't have to be worried about safety, as everyone is guided by a coach throughout the process. As to roller coaster jumping, it is the scariest activity, as you will experience the vertical dropping, so it might be a good choice for those who like extreme sports.

[06:15] AUDIO: Of course, children are not allowed to join in. The last one is the magic show. I'm sure you'll be attracted by the charm of the magician. You can hear the audience burst into applause throughout the show.

[06:28] AUDIO: Please promise me, don't leave early, because just as horror stories won't tell you until the end, there is something unexpected waiting for you. I'm sure you won't regret it. OK, that's all I want to recommend to you today. If you want to know about more fascinating tourist attractions, please wait for our programme next week.
[06:51] AUDIO: Bye!

passages.title: Farmers' attitudes to new developments in agriculture
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Farmers' attitudes to new developments in agriculture"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [01:13] Joel: Dr Owen?
[01:15] Dr. Owen: Come in, Joel. Right, so how's your research going? You're looking at how farmers feel about new technology in agriculture, aren't you?
[01:25] Joel: Well, actually it's more general than that. I'm looking at their attitudes to a variety of new developments in agriculture.
[01:33] Dr. Owen: OK. Have you got a title for the project yet?
[01:37] Joel: I was thinking of something simple, like Farmers' Attitudes Towards the Adoption of New Farming Practices.
[01:46] Dr. Owen: That's possibly a bit too general. I think the title needs to be a bit more specific. What kind of farming will you be looking at?
[01:57] Joel: Well, that'll vary actually. But I want to speak to each of the ten farmers in my sample, so I've chosen farms which are all in the same region.
[02:06] Dr. Owen: OK. Well, I'd specify where they are then.
[02:12] Joel: Right. I'll amend the title to do that.
[02:15] Dr. Owen: OK. Is there any particular reason why you've decided to do face-to-face interviews? It'll be quite time-consuming, won't it?

[02:25] Joel: Yes, and I did consider doing telephone interviews for that reason, especially as it's unnecessary for me to actually see the places where they work. It's just that, in my experience, a lot of farmers don't like talking on the phone, so they'll be more likely to talk freely if I see them in person.
[02:47] Dr. Owen: Yes, you're probably right. Good.
[02:51] Joel: Then the first thing I want to investigate is how the farmers actually find out about new developments in agriculture that they might want to adopt. What sources they use.
[03:03] Dr. Owen: Right. So, how are you going to do this?

[03:07] Joel: Well, I could make a checklist of sources of information for them to look at in advance, so they could tick off the ones they actually use. Things like farming magazines, farm product advertisements, television and the internet and so on.
[03:25] Dr. Owen: It might be more useful to ask them rather than show them a list. A spontaneous response to one or two open questions might give you a more accurate picture.
[03:37] Joel: All right, I'll do that then.
[03:39] Dr. Owen: Now talk me through some of the other issues you want to cover.
[03:43] Joel: Well, there's the way the government communicates with farmers.
[03:48] Dr. Owen: Right. Well, one thing is, farmers complain that the government sends out the same information to all of them, whether they're poultry farmers or dairy farmers or arable farmers.
[04:01] Joel: So they get all this information, but half of it doesn't actually apply to them.
[04:06] Dr. Owen: Exactly. So you could look at that.

[04:10] Joel: Right. Then I wanted to look at attitudes of British farmers to the cost of making any changes on their farms. According to articles I've read, farmers in Britain aren't, in principle, against investing money in new machinery and new practices, but they're actually just too busy to work out what the financial implications are.
[04:35] Dr. Owen: Yes, and a lot of them don't seem to consider getting financial advice from their accountants about it either.
[04:42] Joel: Right.

[04:43] Dr. Owen: There's also been some research in Australia on sheep rearing practices. I can give you the reference, if you like. Basically, it appears that the majority of Australian sheep farmers are willing to risk adopting new practices on the basis of just a few pieces of research. They don't usually wait until the evidence in favour of the changes is overwhelming.
[05:11] Dr. Owen: They're quite happy to act before then so they can get ahead of the game.
[05:16] Joel: OK. I'll take a look at that. Thanks. We said we'd also look at some of the reading material I've been reviewing.
[06:04] Dr. Owen: Yes, I had another look at Contemporary Farming Manual, which is clearly bang up to date. It covers a lot of things a farmer might want to know, but it's so dull.
[06:17] Joel: Absolutely. I found it really hard going and I can't imagine any farmer wading through it. There aren't even any decent pictures.
[06:26] Dr. Owen: Did you have time to look at Running a Small Farm?
[06:30] Joel: Yes, although I only read bits of it because despite being entertaining, it wasn't very academic.
[06:37] Dr. Owen: I know. And a lot of the information is either misleading or simply wrong. I'm surprised it got published at all. I don't imagine the farming press will rate it very highly.
[06:51] Joel: You recommend Agriculture and Economics. I expected that it would be really difficult. The title's a bit off-putting, but I thought it was brilliant. So I've bought it.

[07:04] Dr. Owen: Yes. Some people think it relies too heavily on farming practices in specific parts of the world, but the theories that underpin these are universal, and that's why it's a required textbook for anyone studying agriculture.
[07:21] Joel: Right.
[07:23] Dr. Owen: What else did you come across?
[07:25] Joel: I borrowed How to Survive in Farming from the library. I thought it'd be interesting background, and I liked the informal style, but it turned out to have been written years ago.
[07:37] Dr. Owen: Yes, and like everything else, farming fashions have changed, so it's badly in need of a new edition.
[07:46] Joel: Can I ask you a question about...

transcript: [01:14] AUDIO: Good morning. Over the last few weeks we've been talking about the challenges of producing food for the global population. And there's been a lot of interest recently in new sources of food, and one of the most interesting is insects. Well, why should insects be considered as a food source?

[01:34] AUDIO: Well, for a start, a number of them are full of protein, and many also have certain vitamins, which may surprise you. More so than a typical farm animal, in fact. And compared to farm animals, whose waste products contain a great deal of ammonia, the waste products of insects are far less acidic and would therefore do very little damage to the soil or to any of the rivers that run through farmland. Furthermore, when it comes to the production of insects, the expense would be very low.

[02:05] AUDIO: No trees need be chopped down or forests turned to pasture, so the space that they would occupy would be radically smaller than for, say, cows or sheep. But even if some consumers decided that they'd rather not put insects in their shopping basket, we could also consider how insects might be added to animal feed, the food given to farm animals. It's already known that some insects, if they were part of the animal feed, would act as a sort of natural antibiotic within a cow or sheep's digestive system, thus removing the need for human intervention. This would be a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative for farmers.

[02:52] AUDIO: However, if consumers do decide that insects are a potential superfood, a way of feeding the world, then the next question is where do we source them from? The wild, perhaps? Or should they be bred on insect farms? Well, if we take from the wild, one potential consequence of this is that too many will be taken, and in turn a species could become endangered or extinct.

[03:19] AUDIO: Then, for insects which are harvested from the wild, we have no way of knowing where they have been or what they have come in contact with, and this could have harmful consequences for human health. Imagine the scenario if food producers or retailers were supplied with insects that were carrying bacteria. This is not something we want to add to the food chain. If insects are bred on farms, the problems I've just outlined could be avoided, and in many countries it's already the case that demand for insects is growing, really growing, and it's not in rural areas where you'd expect, but, in fact, in the cities.

[03:58] AUDIO: In Thailand, for example, where the demand has really shot up. However, people in countries where insects are traditionally what people eat, they'll tell you that when insects are intensively farmed, their taste is simply not the same. Ironically, this is the same accusation that people have when it comes to the way that cows and sheep are raised. Insect farmers also face a series of challenges, and researchers are keen to assist.

[04:26] AUDIO: First of all, when it comes to breeding, different insects have different requirements. For a start, it's essential to maintain a suitable temperature for many species to reproduce. If this isn't right, nothing's going to happen. Another problem is something that often happens when any species is bred in a confined space, and so far researchers and farmers have not come up with any clear or long-term effective solution to it.

[04:54] AUDIO: We're talking about the problem of disease. You don't want a whole colony wiped out in one go. There's also the question of where insects need to be kept. If insects are to be bred as a superfood, then the tanks used to house them have to be better designed, and this has to happen so that cleaning takes up less time.

[05:15] AUDIO: If we're talking about mass production, we don't want this to be a time-consuming activity. And finally, like I said before, insects have long been part of the diet in some countries, but not so in others. If farmers want to encourage people in, say, England or France or Germany to eat insects, then they're going to have to develop a strategy, and I'm not talking about production, but marketing. Something that'll persuade potential customers to try something different.
[05:46] AUDIO: Well, I've given you a general overview of the situation. Now let's look at some specific examples.
